## Issue #701 Auto-Learning Adoption Gap

Issue [#701](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/701) (E59) reports
that the auto-learning loop *observed* its own failures without ever adopting a
fix: the Google Trends frontier stayed at 60 unanswered prompts, and a retained
dreaming amendment appended a compliance line without changing how the task was
solved. PR [#817](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/817) closes
the gap end to end — a learning cycle that derives, validates, and proposes;
a ledger that proves each capability delta; and a periodic, human-gated run.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R701-1 | Define the adoption contract: take a frontier item, derive candidate knowledge, validate it against generated tests, and emit a promotion proposal in the exact shape issue #656 consumes. | `rust/src/learning_cycle.rs` implements the cycle; `formal-ai learn cycle --frontier google-trends --dry-run [--proposals]` runs it. Candidates are request-opener surfaces derived from the frozen frontier record, each validated against held-out prompts of the same class before it may be proposed; proposals are rendered by `render_promotion_proposals` and round-trip through `parse_promotion_proposals`. Covered by `the_learning_cycle_emits_promotion_proposals_in_the_issue_656_shape` and `the_cycle_is_deterministic_and_reproducible_offline`. |
| R701-2 | Record a before/after capability pair for every adopted item, in all supported languages. | Implemented: `data/meta/learning-adoption-ledger.lino` records 60 pairs across 10 topics and 4 languages, each with `before_intent "unknown"` and the routed `after_intent`. Generated by `cargo run --release --example issue_701_adoption_ledger` and byte-pinned by `committed_adoption_ledger_matches_a_fresh_run`; the class claim is checked by `the_adoption_ledger_records_a_real_capability_delta_in_every_language`. |
| R701-3 | Drive the issue #498/#499 Trends frontier through the loop until the corpus answers, or record each failure as a named blocking gap. | Implemented: The corpus answers 80/80: `data/meta/google-trends-learning.lino` reports `handled_by_engine "80"` and `learning_frontier "0"`, down from 60 unrouted. The `intent: unknown` rate over the committed corpus fell from 7500 to 0 basis points and is ratcheted by `the_trends_corpus_unknown_rate_is_ratcheted_to_zero`. |
| R701-4 | Dreaming amendments must change solving behaviour through the production path; delete any decoration-only code path. | Delivered: `append_amendments` now reclassifies a covered task instead of only decorating it — a task matched by a retained standing requirement is never returned as unresolved (`STANDING_REQUIREMENT_INTENT`). The three application paths share one selection rule (`matching_amendments`) and one projection (`amendment_lines`); the duplicated `matching_amendment_lines` decorator is deleted. `rust/tests/unit/issue_701_dreaming_amendment_class.rs` raises the single-prompt issue-#540 check to a class-level suite: 3 topics × 4 languages of held-out paraphrases through both protocol surfaces, plus a negative control proving an uncovered task comes back byte-identical. |
| R701-5 | Run the loop periodically in proposal mode by default, honouring the human gate. | `dreaming_runtime::write_learning_cycle_record` leaves a proposal-only record next to the memory log on every idle run, and `.github/workflows/learning-cycle.yml` replays the cycle daily, asserting `mode "proposal_only"`, `human_gated "true"`, and that no seed file changed. Covered by `every_idle_dreaming_run_leaves_a_proposal_only_learning_cycle_record`. |
| R701-6 | Preserve every failure to adopt as a durable frontier record, consistent with R425. | `data/meta/learning-frontier-google-trends.lino` freezes the 60 pre-adoption verdicts even though the live frontier is now empty, and every candidate rejected by its held-out tests is recorded as a blocked class rather than dropped. Covered by `every_failure_to_adopt_is_preserved_as_a_durable_record` and `the_frozen_frontier_record_spans_every_supported_language`. |

## Issue #702 Dialogue World Model

Issue [#702](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/702) (E60, child
of [#651](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/651)) implements the
per-requirement plans issue #649 drafted: PR
[#675](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/675) landed the
substrate (`rust/src/world_model.rs`), but nothing fed it from a conversation. PR
[#818](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/818) adds the dialogue
layer — utterance classification from cue data, a `DialogueWorldModel` that
maintains current/target contexts with provenance and a hash-chained
synchronization log, a chat handler that answers "what is left to do?" from the
current→target difference in all four languages, and a bAbI-style state-tracking
benchmark slice with a ratchet. It also provides one unlimited, explicitly
inherited context hierarchy for dialogue turns, tasks, pull requests, issues,
repositories, and organizations, with lazy nearest-first reference resolution.
The whole feature is **trace-only until opted in**:
`SolverConfig::world_model_mode` defaults to `Off`. The case study lives in
`docs/case-studies/issue-702`.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R702-1 | Seed and maintain the current-state context from the dialogue, with provenance back to the turn that asserted each fact. | Implemented by `DialogueWorldModel::from_turns`/`observe` and `record_provenance` in `rust/src/world_model_dialog.rs`; every asserted atom carries `asserts:<atom>` and `provenance:turn:<n>`. Covered by `rust/tests/unit/issue_702_world_model_dialog.rs`::`declarative_turns_seed_the_current_state_context_with_provenance`. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_702_world_model_dialog.rs`. |
| R702-2 | Build the target-state context from intent formalization: "I want …" statements and imperative requests. | Implemented by `world_model_atoms::classify` over the `world_state_target` cue set in `data/meta/cue-lexicon.lino` (en/ru/hi/zh, no Rust phrase tables) plus `state_atom` extraction. Covered by `rust/tests/unit/issue_702_world_model_dialog.rs`::`wishes_and_requests_build_the_target_state_context` and `all_four_languages_route_the_same_three_utterances_the_same_way`. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_702_world_model_dialog.rs`. |
| R702-3 | Expose `diff(current, target)` as a links network, queryable from chat. | Implemented by `DialogueWorldModel::difference`/`remaining` and the `world_state` contextual handler in `rust/src/solver_handlers/world_state.rs`, which answers `world_state_remaining` / `world_state_reached` and emits `world_state:remaining`, `world_state:difference`, `world_state:sync_events` evidence links. Covered by `rust/tests/unit/issue_702_world_model_dialog.rs`::`the_difference_is_a_links_network_that_answers_what_is_left` and `rust/tests/unit/issue_702_world_state_chat.rs`::`asking_what_is_left_answers_from_the_difference_in_every_language`. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_702_world_model_dialog.rs`. |

## Issue #705 Anticipatory Dreaming

Issue [#705](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/705) (E63)
extends the idle dreaming loop from learning about requests already seen to
preparing for likely next request classes. PR
[#887](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/887) implements a
bounded symbolic model, exhaustive offline probes, proposal-only frontier
integration, consented source capture, offline recall, and later-hit accounting.
The design and preserved source evidence live in
`docs/case-studies/issue-705/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R705-1 | Build inspectable Markov-style transitions over formalized request intent classes from append-only memory, with probability and exact-event provenance rather than raw-text or neural states. | `rust/src/anticipation.rs::plan_anticipation` counts adjacent user-request classes, records `ProbabilityEvidence::MarkovTransition`, and ranks the top three with a stable tie break. Covered by `append_only_intent_transitions_predict_three_next_request_classes`. |
| R705-2 | Expand every top class from the meaning lexicon, operation vocabulary, and observed parameters, probe every member offline, and file every unknown or failed probe on the adoption frontier. | `rust/src/anticipation/expansion.rs` derives bounded variants; `plan_anticipation` uses an offline zero-compute solver and sends the exact failed set through `run_learning_cycle("anticipation", ...)`. Covered by `class_expansion_uses_meaning_operation_and_parameter_evidence` and `every_unknown_or_failed_offline_probe_reaches_the_adoption_frontier`. |
| R705-3 | Prelearn external sources only at idle/lowest priority and with fetch consent, retaining standard source provenance and TTL so future requests can answer offline. | `run_core_dreaming_once` calls `run_idle_anticipation` after its foreground cancellation point; `prelearn_predictions` denies transport without consent and retains URL, fetched time, SHA-256, cache status, and expiry. Covered by `source_prelearning_is_consent_gated_and_uses_cache_provenance_and_ttl`, `idle_dreaming_persists_the_ledger_and_later_live_usage_records_a_hit`, and the held-out capability-delta test. |
| R705-4 | Prediction must never mutate behaviour directly; every proposed rule or seed extension uses the issue-#656 human-gated promotion shape. | Failed probes use the shared issue-#701 cycle and remain `proposal_only` and `human_gated`; no anticipation path writes seed data. Covered by `every_unknown_or_failed_offline_probe_reaches_the_adoption_frontier`. |
| R705-5 | Persist predictions, probes, prelearned captures, and later `prediction_hit` links in an anticipation ledger whose hit rate may honestly begin at 0%. | `AnticipationLedger`, `apply_anticipation`, and `memory_sync::SyncStore` append the records and link a later actual request to its prediction. Covered by `prediction_hits_link_later_actual_requests_and_zero_percent_is_honest` and the idle-runtime integration test. |
| R705-6 | The same history must yield byte-identical predictions and expose why each class was prepared. | Planning uses ordered collections, stable class ids, bounded expansion, and no clock; `why_prediction` and Links Notation expose transition counts and evidence. Covered by `the_same_history_produces_byte_identical_predictions_and_ledger`. |
| R705-7 | A held-out member of a predicted class must change from offline unknown to a correct offline answer after prelearning, without a later fetch, through both compatible response surfaces. | Delivered: `dreaming_application` consults exact, unexpired anticipation aliases only after ordinary solving stays unknown. Covered end to end by `a_held_out_predicted_prompt_becomes_answerable_offline_after_prelearning`. |
| R705-8 | Add the prediction stages to the grounded dreaming recipe and retain issue research, transition design, honest same-task Agent CLI evidence, and release metadata. | `data/meta/dreaming-recipe.lino` now has seventeen contiguous stages; `docs/case-studies/issue-705/`, its byte-pinned self-hosting artifact, `rust/examples/issue_705_anticipatory_dreaming.rs`, and `changelog.d/20260801_140000_anticipatory_dreaming.md` preserve the review trail. Covered by `dreaming_meta_algorithm`, `docs_requirements_issue_705`, and `rust/tests/unit/issue_705_anticipation.rs`. |

## Issue #706 Any-Language Protocol

Issue [#706](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/706) (E64)
records that the four supported languages were coordinated by hand: every
addition touched Rust. PR
[#880](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/880) turns the language
set into one registry of seed data — detection, coverage ledger, generated
round-trip matrix, and CI guards all read the same records.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R706-1 | Adding a language must be a data-only edit: no Rust change for detection, registration, or coverage. | `rust/src/language.rs` embeds `data/seed/language-detection.lino` and derives `Language`, the script table, ranges, markers, and the fallback from it; `Language` is a registry-backed newtype, not an enum. Covered by `issue_706_any_language::detection_registry_is_seed_data_not_rust_constants`. |
| R706-2 | The round-trip contract (language→meta→same language, plus every directed pair) must be generated from the registry, not written per language. | `scripts/language-protocol.mjs` generates `docs/case-studies/issue-706/round-trip-matrix.lino` for all N² pairs; covered by `registry_drives_an_automatically_generated_round_trip_matrix`. |
| R706-3 | A fifth language must pass the generated matrix and at least 80% of the multilingual suite end-to-end. | Implemented: Spanish is registered with `detection_mode script_and_markers` and 1000‰ suite coverage in `docs/case-studies/issue-706/coverage-es.lino`; detection is proved by `fifth_language_is_detected_without_any_rust_change`. |
| R706-4 | Coverage must be honest: a partial language emits `language_gap` instead of a silent English fallback. | `data/seed/languages.lino` declares `fallback_policy explicit_gap`; `seed::localized_response` resolves exact language → the seed's `language unknown` record → English, and every handler uses it. Covered by `a_language_without_localized_openers_reports_a_gap_not_english`. |
| R706-5 | The sixth-language dry run must need no code edit, and CI language parity must extend automatically to every registered language. | `data/language-additions/ar.lino` with `--dry-run` reports `code_changes 0`; `rust/tests/e2e/scripts/check-language-{test-coverage,change-parity}.mjs` discover languages from the ledger. Covered by `sixth_language_dry_run_is_data_only_and_reports_coverage` and `ci_contract_discovers_every_registered_language_from_the_ledger`. |
| R706-6 | The Rust core, the `no_std` WASM worker, and the JS worker must share one detection registry. | Implemented: `rust/src/language.rs` compiles into `js/wasm-worker/src/lib.rs` (re-parsing per call because the bump allocator resets); `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_seed_responses_and_language.js` mirrors `detect_with` over `LANGUAGE_RULES` hydrated from the same seed file by `js/seed_loader.js`. |
| R706-7 | Per-language behaviour outside the detector must also be data: unknown-intent opener pools, display names, concept slugs, and script checks. | `data/seed/unknown-openers.lino` feeds the Rust core, the WASM worker, and the JS worker; `language::language_name`, `language_for_concept_slug`, and `surface_matches_language` read `data/seed/languages.lino` and `language-detection.lino`, replacing the `match` arms in `thinking.rs`, `concepts.rs`, `translation/language_markers.rs`, and `lexeme_import.rs`. Covered by `unknown_openers_are_seed_data_on_every_surface` and `language_metadata_comes_from_the_ledger_not_from_rust_branches`. |
| R706-8 | A new language's request frames must be *learned* from a recorded frontier by the existing issue-#701 cycle, not hand-written. | `rust/src/language_frontier.rs` records `data/meta/learning-frontier-language-gap.lino` by running the live engine over `data/language-additions/*.lino`; `learning_cycle::recorded_frontiers` turns `--frontier` into an open registry so `formal-ai learn cycle --frontier language-gap` replays it through the same cycle. Covered by `the_learn_cli_replays_the_language_frontier_through_the_shared_cycle`. |
| R706-9 | Adoption must be proved as a capability delta, not claimed. | The two validated Spanish frames were adopted as seed data in `data/seed/learned-request-openers.lino`; `data/meta/language-adoption-ledger.lino` pins 7/7 before/after pairs (`unknown_to_web_search`, term recovered, 0 unadopted) and re-recording the frontier now returns `learning_frontier "0"`. Covered by `adopting_the_proposals_changed_what_the_engine_answers` and `re_recording_the_language_frontier_now_finds_nothing_to_learn`. |

## Issue #802 Refutation-First Hypothesis Search

The 2-4-6 lesson is implemented as a domain-independent experiment chooser:
maintain live hypotheses, try to refute them, prefer the probe with the smallest
worst-case survivor set, and report uncertainty when evidence cannot decide.

| ID | Requirement | Status / evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R802-1 | Represent hypotheses, discriminating experiments, observations, and the live hypothesis space as inspectable data. | Implemented by `SearchHypothesis`, `Experiment`, `HypothesisSpace`, and their Links Notation records in `rust/src/selection_heuristics.rs`; pinned by `rust/tests/unit/specification/refutation_search.rs` (`observing_a_result_kills_every_contradicted_hypothesis_and_names_the_experiment`, `every_elimination_is_backed_by_an_evidence_record`). |
| R802-2 | Try to disprove a hypothesis first and select experiments that minimize the worst-case survivors. | Implemented by `attempts_refutation_of`, `worst_case_survivors`, and `RefutationSearch`; covered by the issue #1138 selection tests in `rust/tests/unit/specification/refutation_search.rs` (`the_chosen_experiment_minimizes_worst_case_survivors`, `a_refuting_probe_is_preferred_over_a_confirming_one_at_equal_power`). |
| R802-3 | Use refutation-first search before stochastic sampling when the solver has a discriminating probe. | Implemented by `run_refutation_search` in `rust/src/solver_search.rs`; sampling remains an explicit fallback when no probe discriminates. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/budget_search.rs::budget_search_solves_reachability_under_sufficient_budget`, which requires the solved trace to pass through the registry-backed refutation chooser with evidence-backed eliminations. |
| R802-4 | Feed the search verdict into the reasoning standard and remain honestly undecided when neither side is proved. | Implemented by `hypothesis_search_verdict` in `rust/src/reasoning_standard/mod.rs`; `SearchVerdict::NotConfirmedNotRefuted` preserves the blockers. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1073_reasoning_standard.rs`, which requires an unprobed episode to reach `not_confirmed_not_refuted` with the `hypothesis_search:no_refutation_attempted` blocker. |

## Issue #844 Statement-Level Merging Into A Context

Issue [#844](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/844) asks for
statement-level deduplication, evidence-weighted importance, recursive source
gathering with a recheck before presenting, a merge target that is a context
rather than a list, and an identifier rung below the topic rung. PR
[#855](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/855) implements all of
it through the exact-capture and named fact-checking boundaries delivered by
issues #843 and #845. `SourceProvider` remains only as a deterministic fixture
seam. See `docs/case-studies/issue-844/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R501 | Deduplicate at the statement level so N sources asserting one fact yield one fact, each merge recorded as an explainable link. | Implemented by `rust/src/summarization/dedup.rs` (`StatementSignature`, `MergedStatement`, `MergeLink`); covered by `n_sources_asserting_one_fact_yield_one_statement_with_a_justification_link`. |
| R502 | Stay conservative: merge wording differences only, never stem, so a different inflection or extra content stays a separate fact (`NON-GOALS.md:39`). | Implemented by the content-term signature over seed-known function words; covered by `wording_differences_merge_but_extra_content_does_not` and `inflected_wordings_stay_separate_because_the_merge_does_not_stem`. |
| R503 | Make every merge reversible, so a merge that conflates two facts can be split back into its variants. | Implemented by `DedupReport::split`; covered by `a_merge_that_conflates_two_facts_can_be_split`. |
| R504 | Weight importance by evidence: the kind prior blended with observed link frequency, source authority, and stance, with unoriginal mirrors adding neither probability nor ranking evidence. | Implemented by `rust/src/summarization/importance.rs`; covered by `ranking_reflects_observed_frequency_and_source_stance`, `an_unoriginal_mirror_adds_no_probability`, and `unoriginal_repetition_cannot_outrank_an_authoritative_source`. |
| R505 | Gather sources recursively from the unmet difference, bounded by depth and terminating at a fixpoint. | Implemented by `rust/src/summarization/gathering.rs` (`GatheringPlan`, `gather`); covered by three gathering tests including a citation cycle and an endless chain. |
| R506 | Cache every fetch content-addressed and per URL, so a warm cache replays byte-identically without reaching the provider or inheriting another URL's tier. | Implemented by `SourceCache` (digest-keyed bodies, one entry per URL); covered by `a_warm_cache_replays_the_same_gathering_without_fetching`. |
| R507 | Recheck before presenting: an unsupported statement is withheld from the summary while staying in the context. | Implemented by `rust/src/summarization/recheck.rs` and `MergedContext::checked_summary`; covered by `a_statement_no_trusted_source_asserts_is_withheld_but_kept`. |
| R508 | Merge into a `world_model::Context`: a probability per statement, contradictions as mutual `Contradicts` edges, disagreement reported rather than resolved, and no fabricated consensus between two original sources that disagree. | Implemented by `rust/src/summarization/context.rs` plus the cycle-collapse fixpoint in `Context::recalculate`; covered by `contradictions_become_contradicts_edges_and_are_reported_as_disagreement` and `a_saturated_mutual_contradiction_settles_at_maximal_uncertainty`. |
| R509 | Extend the summarization ladder downward with an identifier rung honouring syntactic constraints, a length budget, and naming conventions. | Implemented by `rust/src/summarization/identifier.rs` and `SummarizationMode::Identifier`; covered by `the_identifier_rung_produces_valid_identifiers_under_a_length_budget` and `the_identifier_rung_is_the_bottom_of_the_ladder`. |
| R510 | Run the Stack Overflow case end to end, deterministically and without neural inference (`NON-GOALS.md:7`, `GOALS.md:54`), with case-study traceability and release metadata. | Implemented by `rust/examples/issue_844_statement_merge.rs`, `docs/case-studies/issue-844/`, and the changelog fragment; covered by `the_stack_overflow_case_works_end_to_end`, `the_merge_is_deterministic_and_independent_of_source_order`, and `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements/statement_merging.rs`. |

## Issue #873 Research-Driven Unknown Recovery

Issue [#873](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/873) makes an
unknown a research frontier and gives research, learning, verification, and
recovery one shared lifecycle. The full source analysis, alternatives, online
research, and raw issue data live in `docs/case-studies/issue-873/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R873-1 | Every unresolved online input must trigger research and still produce an evidence-backed answer. | Implemented by the general fallback in `rust/src/solver_unknown_reasoning.rs` and the intent-driven agentic handoff in `rust/src/agentic_coding/web_research.rs`; the direct, tool-call, and search→fetch→answer proofs are in `rust/tests/unit/unresolved_request_research.rs`. Explicit offline mode retains the diagnostic unknown boundary. |
| R873-2 | Use reachable internet/local observations and allow recomputable payloads to be evicted and recollected without losing provenance. | Delivered: `research_learning::SourceReceipt` retains locator/content identity separately from its optional payload. `evict_source` drops only recomputable payloads; `recollect_source` restores an identity match and changed data becomes a new receipt. |
| R873-3 | Version memory, retain its history, recover every tested stable state, and leave the prior stable version running when a candidate fails compilation or tests. | Delivered: `KnowledgeVersion` is parent-linked and append-only; candidate/stable/rejected states are separate from the active stable pointer. `verify_candidate` never activates a failed proposal and `recover_stable` moves only to a previously stable version. |
| R873-4 | Keep most gates immutable and never switch unless the complete baseline passes. | Delivered: Promotion requires every gate to pass, every configured baseline id to be immutable, and immutable gates to form a strict majority. Exact rejection/promotion/incomplete-baseline tests pin all three conditions. |
| R873-5 | Convert any error into a recovery path instead of becoming stuck. | Delivered: `recover_from_error` accepts every error id and supplies `restore_stable_and_research` when no caller-provided alternative exists; its transition is retained in the hash-linked cycle history. |
| R873-6 | Ask the user when recovery is ambiguous; in full-trust mode rank prior advantages and disadvantages and select automatically. | Delivered: `AskOnAmbiguity` returns the deterministically ordered alternatives; `FullTrust` transparently scores prior successes, failures, advantages, and disadvantages; `PerCommand` returns a permission request. |
| R873-7 | Bound work at a configurable one-hour default, return the current plan, and require continuation permission while supporting full autonomy and per-command approval. | Delivered: `DEFAULT_RESEARCH_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS` is 3,600 and is shared with external-agent orchestration defaults. `check_time_limit` returns `AwaitingContinuation { current_plan }`; `continue_with_permission` is the explicit resumption boundary. |
| R873-8 | Express the architecture as one general meta-algorithm that can append/generalize itself. | Delivered: `ResearchLearningCycle` applies one reducer to facts, procedures, and `MetaAlgorithm` versions. `data/meta/research-learning-recovery.lino` records its ordered phases, and changes to that recipe pass through the same proposal, immutable gate, promotion, and recovery logic. |
| R873-9 | Preserve all issue data, enumerate every requirement, research primary external sources and related components, and compare solution plans in a deep case study. | Implemented in `docs/case-studies/issue-873/README.md`, `requirements.md`, `online-research.md`, `raw-data/`, and the same-task authorship record. |
| R873-10 | Complete the plan in one pull request. | Code, data, tests, example, architecture/requirement documentation, changelog, and evidence are delivered together by PR #983. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/unresolved_request_research.rs::the_plan_landed_with_its_data_example_documentation_and_release_note`. |

## Issue #901 TRIZ Contradictions

Trade-offs are represented as inspectable links between satisfying candidates.
The selected point is derived from criterion-bearing requirement clauses; it is
never an unexplained default at fifty percent. The reusable principles remain
seed data so they can be forgotten and rediscovered without changing code.

| ID | Requirement | Status / evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R901-1 | Represent each technical contradiction as a link between candidates and expose a selection value from 0 to 1. | Implemented by `ContradictionLink.selection_basis_points` and its Links Notation rendering in `rust/src/selection_heuristics.rs`; covered by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_selection_heuristics.rs`. |
| R901-2 | Derive the selection point from explicit criteria instead of silently choosing a midpoint. | Implemented by `contradictions_in`: requirement clauses or a cited seed record supply `ContradictionDerivation`; otherwise the result is `Underivable` and remains unresolved. |
| R901-3 | Make contradiction resolution a registry-selected ranking method rather than a separate hard-coded route. | Delivered, 2026-10-08. `data/meta/selection-heuristics.lino` now declares `heuristic_triz` at role `rank`, order 3, with `applies_when contradiction_detected`. `draft_portfolio.rs::rank_passing_drafts` and `algorithm_discovery/ranking.rs::rank_survivors` both call `contradictions_in` to detect the situation and resolve their ranker through `heuristics_for(HeuristicRole::Rank, situation)`, selecting `TrizRanker` at order 3 when a contradiction is detected and keeping `LeastActionRanker` for every other situation. The JavaScript twin `js/agentic/crate/selection_heuristics_triz.mjs` mirrors `contradictions_in`, `TrizRanker`, and the registry selection (`rankWithHeuristic`, `situationFor`). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/specification/triz_contradictions.rs` (seeded row, registry selection, ranker disagreement on the contradicted pair) and `rust/tests/web/issue-0901-triz-registry.test.mjs` (JS parity). |
| R901-4 | Preserve the 40 inventive principles and four separation principles as source-linked, forgettable knowledge. | Implemented by `data/seed/triz-principles.lino`; the forget-and-rediscover regression is in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_selection_heuristics.rs`. |
| R901-5 | Validate the mechanism on at least 20 distinct tasks. | Implemented by the 20-case, five-language corpus in `data/benchmarks/selection-triz.lino`; every declared relation is derived and checked by `the_twenty_task_triz_corpus_derives_each_declared_selection_relation`. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_selection_heuristics.rs`. |

seed-defined projections instead of direct language-pair translators.

| R917-2 | Formal targets, natural word order, and canonical relation surfaces must be seed-defined projections of one semantic statement, not per-pair translators. | Delivered: `data/seed/formal-language-projections.lino` defines the projection catalog; `rust/src/translation/formal_statement.rs` interprets it as one parser and one renderer per syntax. | R917-4 | Native and browser surfaces must expose the same natural-formal translation behavior. | Delivered: `whole_task_translation_uses_the_formal_projection_in_both_directions` covers the native engine; `rust/tests/e2e/tests/formal-language-projections.spec.js` covers both directions for every seed language through the Rust-to-WASM worker. |
| R917-5 | Adding another formal target or natural projection must remain a data change. | Delivered: The projection interpreters use the catalog's formal alias, statement template, word order, and relation surface; no source/target pair table is present. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/formal_projection_round_trips.rs::projection_catalog_is_seed_data_and_the_interpreter_names_no_projection`, which fails if the interpreter names any projection slug the seed declares. |
| R917-6 | Issue, PR, related-work, research, requirements, plan, architecture, roadmap, and release evidence must remain traceable. | Delivered: `issue_917_case_study_and_release_metadata_are_traceable` guards `docs/case-studies/issue-917`, the root documents, raw snapshots, and the minor changelog fragment. |

## Issue #933 Conversational Wording-Variation Floor

Issue [#933](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/933) is the CI
enforcement that issue
[#123](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/123) asked for and
PR [#124](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/124) did not deliver:
every conversational test case must hold at least five distinct wording
variations in each of `en`, `ru`, `hi` and `zh`. The corpus is data
(`data/benchmarks/conversational-variations-suite.lino` plus its per-language
partitions), the count is a CI gate
(`rust/tests/e2e/scripts/check-conversational-variation-floor.mjs`), and every
recorded prompt is answered by the real engine
(`rust/tests/unit/conversational_variations.rs`). Evidence, the "before" measurement
and the dedup analysis against the existing language checks are in
[`docs/case-studies/issue-933/`](../../case-studies/issue-933/README.md). The
requirement IDs below are the ones used in that case study.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R933-1 | "Wording variation" is machine-checkable, not a convention in comments. | Implemented: a manifest declares the cases, the languages and `minimum_variations_per_language`, and each prompt is a `conversational_variation_case` record carrying its case, language, expected intent, expected evidence link and expected answer. The Agent-authored contract in `data/meta/conversational-variation-floor-contract.lino` defines the equivalence rule: NFKC then lowercase, discard Unicode punctuation/symbol/separator categories and whitespace, and preserve letters, numbers and combining marks. Covered by `rust/tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs` (the manifest and record parsers) and `rust/tests/unit/issue_933_self_authoring.rs::issue_933_formal_ai_authored_contract_is_preserved_byte_for_byte`. |
| R933-2 | A CI script walks the corpus and fails if any test case holds fewer than five variations in any advertised language. | Implemented: `npm run --prefix rust/tests/e2e check:variation-floor`. It also rejects duplicate ids, unlisted cases or languages, records in the wrong partition, prompts that are empty once punctuation is stripped, prompts that only re-punctuate one already counted, and records that show no answer. Covered by `rust/tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs`, one test per rejection. |
| R933-3 | Under-covered cases are backfilled until the check passes. | Implemented: 10 cases × 4 languages, 228 prompts, smallest group 5. The router phrasings the backfill needed were added to `data/seed/intent-routing.lino` and `data/seed/meanings-intent.lino`; 8 of 24 groups in the previous corpus were below the floor (`docs/case-studies/issue-933/raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt`). Covered by `rust/tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs::the committed corpus clears the floor and prints its count table on success`, which runs the gate over the committed corpus and asserts the `10 cases x 4 languages, 228 verified prompts` line. |
| R933-4 | The check runs in CI. | Implemented: `data/meta/ci-gates/check-conversational-variation-floor.lino`, stage `web`, run by `rust-script scripts/run-ci-gates.rs --stage web` from `.github/workflows/release.yml` (issue #991 replaced the workflow's step list with this registry). Covered by `rust/tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs::the gate is registered as a web-stage CI gate that runs the npm script`. |
| R933-5 | A unit test covers the counting logic with fixture data engineered to trip the floor. | Implemented: `rust/tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs` — a group at four, a language with no records at all, five re-punctuated copies of one phrase that must count as one, and a record that shows no answer. |
| R933-6 | Manual check: reducing one case to four variations in one language fails locally. | Implemented: `docs/case-studies/issue-933/raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt` (Node gate, exit 1) and `rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt` (the Rust half of the same deletion). The same deletion now runs on every CI pass: `rust/tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs::removing one Hindi wording fails the gate and names exactly that case` copies the gate and corpus, drops `assistant_name_hi_05`, and asserts exit 1. |
| R933-7 | Coverage counts print per language on every run. | Implemented: the count table prints on success as well as failure — `docs/case-studies/issue-933/raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt`. Covered by `rust/tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs`: the success run asserts the table header and its ten rows, the failure run the `assistant_name` row at `5 5 4 5`. |
| R933-8 | A failure names exactly which cases are under the floor. | Implemented: one `- case <name> has <n> <language> variation(s); the floor is 5` line per shortfall, followed by the file to edit. Covered by `rust/tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs::removing one Hindi wording fails the gate and names exactly that case`, which asserts the exact failure lines. |
| R933-9 | Standing clauses: a case study under `docs/case-studies/issue-933/`, delivered as a single pull request. | Implemented: the case study and PR [#1010](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1010). Covered by `rust/tests/unit/issue_933_self_authoring.rs::issue_933_documents_every_requirement`, which requires every R933 id in both the case study and this shard. |
| R933-10 | The new gate does not duplicate `check:language-test-coverage`. | Implemented as a recorded comparison: that gate is diff-aware and satisfied by one mention of each registered language in a pull request's added test lines; it can never observe a case stuck at four wordings. Full comparison against it, `check:language-change-parity` and `check:intent-coverage` in the case study, kept there by `rust/tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs::the case study records why the floor does not duplicate the existing language gates (R933-10)`. |
| R933-11 | Every recorded variation is one the engine actually routes, and it shows the exact answer that wording produces. | Implemented: `rust/tests/unit/conversational_variations.rs` answers all 228 prompts with `FormalAiEngine` and asserts intent, evidence link and the recorded `expected_answer` verbatim (`expected_answer_contains` for the multi-paragraph capability listing and for arithmetic values). Counting alone cannot be satisfied with wordings the router rejects, and a corpus that records answers is documentation as well as a floor (R234-2). |
| R933-12 | The recorded answers are complete in every advertised language. | Implemented (a fix): recording the answers surfaced sixteen Hindi and Chinese prompts answering with an empty string, and Russian and Hindi wellbeing answers losing their closing sentence, while English was untouched. Root cause in `rust/src/question_necessity.rs` (a sentence boundary required whitespace after the stop and did not know the Devanagari danda; corner brackets and parentheses did not shield a quoted example) and in `data/seed/question-necessity.lino` (requirement cues covered the English follow-ups only). Regression test: `rust/tests/unit/issue_933_answer_parity.rs`, five tests that all fail on the unfixed engine, plus a sixth pinning the Spanish seed answers, which the floor does not cover because `es` is registered `status partial`. |
| R933-13 | Execute part of the issue through Formal AI and the real Agent CLI: attempt the whole task, split only from failure until the leaves are solvable, climb back up, and learn from those same sessions without self-promotion. | Implemented: `experiments/issue_933_self_authoring/run.sh` captures five real Agent-CLI sessions in `docs/case-studies/issue-933/self-hosting-authorship/`: whole failure, three passing leaves, passing parent retry. Two of six deliverable leaves are Formal-AI-authored (33%). `rust/src/orchestration/incremental.rs` now feeds every run's exact sessions to proposal-only client-contract learning; this run's `learning.lino` reports five observations and four `awaiting_human_review` proposals. `rust/tests/unit/issue_933_self_authoring.rs` and `rust/tests/integration/issue_991_incremental_dispatch.rs` pin the artifact and general lifecycle. |
| R933-14 | Node and Rust implement the normalization contract identically for compatibility characters and combining marks. | Implemented (a fix): both now apply NFKC before lowercase, discard the same Unicode P/S/Z category families and whitespace, and preserve combining marks. Both regression suites assert `Ａ == A`, `１ == 1`, `ϒ == υ`, and `क != का`; the Greek pair makes the operation order observable, while the earlier Rust implementation disagreed on the fullwidth examples and collapsed the Hindi pair. Covered by `rust/tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs` (normalization folds case, punctuation and spacing) and its Rust twin `rust/tests/unit/conversational_variations.rs::conversational_variation_normalization_matches_the_unicode_ci_convention`. |

## Issue #982 Persisted-Memory Compatibility Contract

Issue [#982](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/982) requires a
safe upgrade boundary for long-lived `.lino` memory shared by CLI, server,
desktop, Telegram, and container deployments. The schema contract lives in
`rust/src/memory/upgrade.rs`; operator guidance is in
`docs/configuration/memory.md`; regression and container coverage is in
`rust/tests/integration/issue_982_memory_upgrade.rs` and
`experiments/issue_982_memory_upgrade/run_container_upgrade.sh`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R982-1 | Preflight compatibility must be machine-readable and must not mutate memory or create migration artifacts. | Implemented by `formal-ai memory upgrade-status --format json` / `preflight_memory_upgrade`; `upgrade_status_detects_released_schema_without_mutating_memory` asserts byte equality and a one-entry directory. Pinned by `rust/tests/integration/issue_982_memory_upgrade.rs`. JavaScript twin: `node js/server/main.mjs memory upgrade-status` and `memory migrate` (`js/server/memory-upgrade.mjs`), pinned case for case by `rust/tests/web/server-memory-upgrade.test.mjs`. |
| R982-2 | Persist and report explicit detected, minimum-readable, maximum-readable, and target schema versions. | Implemented: schema 1 names released unversioned `demo_memory`; schema 2 adds the root marker. `formal-ai memory upgrade-status --format json` and `/health` (Rust, and the JavaScript server's `memoryHealthStatus`) expose the detected, minimum-readable, maximum-readable, and target schema versions and the migration state. Pinned by `rust/tests/integration/issue_982_memory_upgrade.rs` (`upgrade_status_detects_released_schema_without_mutating_memory`, `health_exposes_schema_compatibility_without_triggering_migration`) and `rust/tests/web/server-memory-schema.test.mjs`. JavaScript twin: `node js/server/main.mjs memory upgrade-status` and `memory migrate` (`js/server/memory-upgrade.mjs`), pinned case for case by `rust/tests/web/server-memory-upgrade.test.mjs`. |
| R982-3 | Upgrades must be explicit; startup, health, ordinary reads, and ordinary writes must never silently migrate an existing file. | Implemented: `MemoryStore` and `SyncStore` (and the JavaScript `SyncStore`) retain the detected source schema on save, a new store starts at the target schema, and only `memory migrate` moves an existing file to schema 2. Pinned by `rust/tests/integration/issue_982_memory_upgrade.rs` (`ordinary_server_write_preserves_released_schema_and_unknown_metadata`, `first_write_to_a_new_store_uses_the_target_schema`, `health_exposes_schema_compatibility_without_triggering_migration`) and `rust/tests/web/server-memory-schema.test.mjs`. |
| R982-4 | Migration must coordinate with ordinary writers and reject incompatible/future schemas without modifying them. | Implemented: `migrate_memory` holds the sibling `fs2` writer lock for the whole transaction and fails closed; a held lock, a future schema (99), and malformed memory each return a nonzero JSON refusal and leave the file byte-identical, and both servers refuse ordinary writes to an incompatible file. Pinned by `rust/tests/integration/issue_982_memory_upgrade.rs` (`live_writer_lock_causes_machine_readable_refusal_without_modification`, `future_schema_is_refused_nonzero_and_never_modified`, `malformed_memory_is_refused_nonzero_and_never_modified`) and `rust/tests/web/server-memory-schema.test.mjs`. JavaScript twin: `node js/server/main.mjs memory upgrade-status` and `memory migrate` (`js/server/memory-upgrade.mjs`), pinned case for case by `rust/tests/web/server-memory-upgrade.test.mjs`. Its lock is the same `flock`, held by a `perl` helper process because Node has none; JavaScript-server ordinary writes create the lock file without holding it. |
| R982-5 | Create and verify a byte-exact rollback backup before commit. | Implemented: the migration writes the backup, re-reads it, and checks both bytes and SHA-256 before staging; it preserves source permissions, refuses a pre-existing backup holding other bytes (`backup_conflict`, both files untouched), and records the backup path and both digests in the receipt. Pinned by `rust/tests/integration/issue_982_memory_upgrade.rs` (`migration_is_atomic_lossless_receipted_idempotent_and_rollback_safe`, `conflicting_backup_is_refused_and_the_default_backup_is_content_addressed`). JavaScript twin: `node js/server/main.mjs memory upgrade-status` and `memory migrate` (`js/server/memory-upgrade.mjs`), pinned case for case by `rust/tests/web/server-memory-upgrade.test.mjs`. |
| R982-6 | Commit atomically and make interruption/retry safe and idempotent. | Implemented: same-directory create-new staging, `sync_all`, atomic rename, parent sync, cleanup on the pre-commit interruption hook, a default backup named by the source digest (a retry re-verifies the same file), and a target-schema no-op retry. Pinned by `rust/tests/integration/issue_982_memory_upgrade.rs` (`interrupted_migration_keeps_original_byte_identical_and_retryable`, `migration_is_atomic_lossless_receipted_idempotent_and_rollback_safe`, `conflicting_backup_is_refused_and_the_default_backup_is_content_addressed`). JavaScript twin: `node js/server/main.mjs memory upgrade-status` and `memory migrate` (`js/server/memory-upgrade.mjs`), pinned case for case by `rust/tests/web/server-memory-upgrade.test.mjs`. |
| R982-7 | Preserve unknown metadata, stable identifiers, event ordering, and history. | Implemented: migration inserts only the additive root marker, and event parsing/formatting round-trips unknown fields in both runtimes. Pinned by `rust/tests/integration/issue_982_memory_upgrade.rs` (the whole-flow case compares exact bytes apart from the marker and checks ids, order, extensions, query, and export; `released_writer_escapes_are_valid_upgrade_input_and_round_trip_losslessly`) and `rust/tests/web/server-memory-schema.test.mjs`. JavaScript twin: `node js/server/main.mjs memory upgrade-status` and `memory migrate` (`js/server/memory-upgrade.mjs`), pinned case for case by `rust/tests/web/server-memory-upgrade.test.mjs`. |
| R982-8 | Emit a durable machine-readable migration receipt with rollback instructions. | Implemented: `MemoryMigrationReceipt` carries binary and schema versions, migration id, memory/backup/receipt paths, before/after SHA-256, event count, changed flag, and rollback strategy; it is written durably beside the memory (or to `--receipt`) and printed on stdout. Pinned by `rust/tests/integration/issue_982_memory_upgrade.rs`: the receipt equals its exact expected value, the file equals stdout, and a no-op retry reports `not_required`. JavaScript twin: `node js/server/main.mjs memory upgrade-status` and `memory migrate` (`js/server/memory-upgrade.mjs`), pinned case for case by `rust/tests/web/server-memory-upgrade.test.mjs`. |
| R982-9 | Provide fixtures for every readable/released schema and reject an intentionally incompatible fixture. | Implemented: `rust/tests/fixtures/memory/schema-{1,2}.lino` cover every readable schema and are enumerated by `fixtures_cover_every_readable_schema` and by the JavaScript twin, which also asserts no other schema fixture exists; the schema-99 case verifies status and migration refusals. Pinned by `rust/tests/integration/issue_982_memory_upgrade.rs` and `rust/tests/web/server-memory-schema.test.mjs`. JavaScript twin: `node js/server/main.mjs memory upgrade-status` and `memory migrate` (`js/server/memory-upgrade.mjs`), pinned case for case by `rust/tests/web/server-memory-upgrade.test.mjs`. |
| R982-10 | Prove a previous released container and candidate container can use the same named volume through upgrade, verification, rollback, and old-version reopen. | Implemented by `experiments/issue_982_memory_upgrade/run_container_upgrade.sh`, which `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs after building the candidate image: it writes with the released `0.335.0` image, preflights and migrates with the candidate, checks candidate query/export and server `/health`, restores the verified backup, and reopens it with `0.335.0`. The two-image run needs Docker and the published image, so it executes in CI; `rust/tests/integration/issue_982_memory_upgrade.rs` (`container_upgrade_harness_runs_in_ci_from_released_write_to_released_reopen`) pins the wiring and the stage order, and `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/docker_resource_hygiene.rs` its container cleanup. |
| R982-11 | Keep implementation provenance and self-hosting evidence reproducible. | Implemented: the issue/PR evidence collector outputs are committed with a manifest under `docs/case-studies/issue-982/raw-data/github/`; two differently worded real Agent-CLI runs and deterministic session JSON live under `docs/case-studies/issue-982/self-hosting/` and are replayed byte-for-byte by `rust/tests/integration/issue_982_self_hosting.rs`. |

## Issue #991 Dynamic Multi-Source How-To Synthesis

Issue [#991](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/991) is the
remainder of [#710](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/710)
row 20 after #444/PR #448 delivered the discovery plan and #709/PR #884 delivered
the source-tier and contradiction policy: a procedural request has to return the
guide the plan describes. `rust/src/how_to_guide.rs` (with `extract.rs`,
`render.rs`), `rust/src/service_accessibility.rs`, and the browser mirror
`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_memory_inspection.js` execute one bounded selection and
synthesis contract; `rust/tests/fixtures/issue-991/` holds the committed real-service
captures the native, HTTP, and browser suites replay offline. The before/after
evidence, root causes, and the known lexical-relevance limitation are in
`docs/case-studies/issue-991/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R991-1 | The Rust/server and browser-worker production paths execute the same bounded source-selection and guide-synthesis contract. | Implemented: `rust/src/how_to_guide.rs` and `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_memory_inspection.js` order accepted steps by source tier, depth, source, then position under the same `GuideBounds`. Both are checked against one recorded expectation, `rust/tests/fixtures/issue-991/expected-guides.json`, written from the Rust path by `rust/examples/issue_991_how_to_parity.rs` — `rust/tests/unit/issue_991_how_to_synthesis.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-991-how-to-synthesis.test.mjs` fail on any drift. |
| R991-2 | Every enabled relevant service from `sources-registry.lino` can contribute, and settings opt-outs remain authoritative. | Implemented: candidate services are read from `data/seed/sources-registry.lino` (`service_group external_trusted`) rather than hardcoded, and a service whose `settings_key` is opted out is reported as `disabled` with zero pages and zero steps and is never contacted, cached or not. Pinned natively and over HTTP by `chat_completions_honours_a_service_opt_out` in `rust/tests/integration/issue_991_how_to_http.rs`. |
| R991-3 | Search results are captured recursively within declared depth/page/time bounds, and every accepted step retains exact provenance. | Implemented: a relevant Stack Exchange question at depth 0 is followed to its answers at depth 1 and a listless wiki page to its same-wiki links, all inside `max_depth=2 max_pages_per_service=4 max_services=4 max_steps=12` with a capture-age bound. Each step keeps its source id, exact URL, license, sha256 digest, and depth, and the rendered guide states the bounds it ran under. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_991_how_to_synthesis.rs` (`search_results_are_captured_recursively_within_the_depth_bound`, `every_accepted_step_carries_exact_provenance_within_declared_bounds`). |
| R991-4 | Conflicts, copied sources, and insufficient evidence use the #709 source-tier and contradiction policy. | Implemented: contradicting steps are reported under `### Conflicts`, mirrored bodies under `### Copied sources ignored`, and a run below `MIN_ACCEPTED_STEPS` renders `Insufficient evidence` instead of a procedure — `chat_completions_reports_insufficient_evidence_instead_of_inventing_steps` proves an undocumented task asserts no step and carries no digest. Pinned by `rust/tests/integration/issue_991_how_to_http.rs`. |
| R991-5 | Per-service accessibility success *and* failure is stored in the environment associative memory with a TTL of at least seven days, with explicit refresh/invalidation. | Implemented: `rust/src/service_accessibility.rs` records both outcomes with `TTL = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60` seconds and exposes `needs_refresh`, `invalidate`, and `invalidate_all`; a failure on a fallback endpoint is recorded as `fallback_failed` so it does not condemn a service whose entry endpoint works. The record round-trips through `service-accessibility.lino` in the cache directory. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_991_how_to_synthesis.rs`::`per_service_accessibility_is_remembered_for_at_least_seven_days` and its browser twin in `rust/tests/web/issue-991-how-to-synthesis.test.mjs`. |
| R991-6 | Real-service QA captures are committed with timestamps, hashes, and licenses; the normal suite replays them offline and a gated refresh check detects drift. | Implemented: `rust/tests/fixtures/issue-991/capture-manifest.lino` records each capture's timestamp, sha256, byte count, and license. With the transport disabled the suite replays them deterministically; `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_FETCH=1` re-fetches through the same production path and reports drift. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_991_how_to_synthesis.rs` (`the_committed_captures_replay_offline_and_match_their_digests`, `the_gated_refresh_check_detects_drift_against_the_real_services`). |
| R991-7 | Minimal native, HTTP agent/API, and browser regressions fail before the implementation and pass through the real production paths afterwards. | Implemented: `rust/tests/unit/issue_991_how_to_synthesis.rs` (native), `rust/tests/integration/issue_991_how_to_http.rs` (a real `formal-ai serve` process answering over `/api/openai/v1/chat/completions`), and `rust/tests/web/issue-991-how-to-synthesis.test.mjs` (browser worker). `docs/case-studies/issue-991/raw-data/before-fix-run.txt` shows a binary built at this branch's base commit answering the same request with the discovery plan and no steps, sources, or digests. |
| R991-8 | No file in this repository is a shared append point that two branches must both edit, so the probability of a merge conflict on it is structurally zero rather than merely reduced. | Implemented: `scripts/analyze-merge-conflicts.py --ledger` measures every historical conflict into `data/meta/merge-conflict-ledger.lino`; `data/meta/merge-conflict-policy.lino` is the reviewed registry of which paths are `merge=union` and which normalizer restores each one; `rust-script scripts/check-merge-conflict-policy.rs` fails while the ledger, `.gitattributes`, and the registry disagree. The three measured causes are each removed at the source: shared sources and append-only lists become one file per entry (`docs/requirements/`, `data/meta/ci-gates/`, `data/meta/worker-line-budget/`), and derived artifacts are regenerated by `scripts/regenerate-derived-artifacts.sh` instead of hand-merged. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_991_merge_conflict_policy.rs`: CI runs the checker and its own tests, every `merge=union` path has a reviewed registry entry, and the formerly shared lists are one file per entry. |
| R991-9 | A task too large for one agent CLI session is split from its own recorded failure, not from a plan committed to before any evidence existed, and an irreducible failure is reported for review instead of retried forever. | Implemented: `TaskExecutor::split` (`rust/src/recursive_execution.rs`) is answered by `formal_ai::task_decomposition::SplittingExecutor` with the repository's own `decompose_task`, one level per split and bounded by `DEFAULT_SPLIT_DEPTH_BOUND`; a child that repeats its parent is refused. `formal-ai agent dispatch --incremental` (`rust/src/orchestration/incremental.rs`) runs that protocol against real CLIs, applies a passing attempt's effects before the next attempt starts, escalates an irreducible failure to the next `--cli`, and reports every attempt, split, and blocked task in the `incremental` trace. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_991_incremental_decomposition.rs` and, through real processes, `rust/tests/integration/issue_991_incremental_dispatch.rs`. |

## Issue #1138 Composition From Retrieved Sources

Retrieved procedure text — not an enumerated shape catalog — is the source of
coding answers. The steps are formalized into a language-neutral IR and lowered
per language; the seeded idiom catalog that bootstrapped this path is itself
deletable data whose loss is provably recoverable. The contract is covered by
`rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/` (procedure text, program IR, IR lowering,
composition search, multilingual parity) and the full-suite upstream rows in
`data/benchmarks/external-results.lino`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1138-B2-1 | Retrieved procedure text becomes an ordered, typed step list with per-step source spans, never a stored answer body. | Implemented by `coding_discovery::procedure_text`; covered by `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/procedure_text.rs`. |
| R1138-B2-2 | The ordered step list lowers into a language-neutral `ProgramIr` whose nodes carry types, fragments, grounding, and license metadata. | Implemented by `rust/src/coding/program_ir.rs`; covered by `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/program_ir.rs`. |
| R1138-B2-3 | The `ProgramIr` renders per target language — the lowerer is selected after composition and preserves the IR identity — and equivalent requirements in English, Russian, Hindi, Chinese, and Spanish expose the same frontier. | Implemented by IR lowering and Python rendering; covered by `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/ir_lowering.rs` and the 25 held-out cases in `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/multilingual.rs`. |
| R1138-B2-4 | The seeded idiom catalog is a deletable bootstrap: every fragment is declared `bootstrap true` with a rediscovery query, and deleting it loses no source evidence. | Implemented by `data/seed/coding-composition-fragments.lino`; covered by `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/fragment_catalog.rs`. |
| R1138-B2-5 | Forgetting a discovered procedure and rediscovering it from the same trusted sources reproduces the same content id. | Implemented by the discovered-procedure ledger; covered by `forgotten_procedures_are_rediscovered_from_the_same_sources` in `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/ledger.rs`. |
| R1138-B2-6 | The upstream coding suites are measured at full slice (HumanEval 164, MBPP 500), online and cold-offline, with per-slice floors and the recorded failure frontier — a first-20 score is a regression control, never a suite score. | Implemented: measured by `benchmark run --suite humaneval --slice 164` and `--suite mbpp --slice 500`, each cold-offline and with `--online`; rows recorded 2026-09-17 in `data/benchmarks/external-results.lino` with `--frontier-record`; floors enforced as best-measured pass counts by `external_benchmarks::ratchet`, verified by `rust/tests/unit/specification/external_benchmarks.rs`. |
| R1138-B2-7 | Every held-out structural answer reports a `typed_search(…)` composition over seed fragments, and no benchmark identifier, task sentence, assertion, or expected-output literal may leak into source or seed data — an example's expected value is payable only as a conditional branch payload, never as a condition operand. | Covered by `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/structural_composition.rs` and `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/no_memorization.rs`; the observation-literal slot filter is enforced in `rust/src/coding/composition_search.rs`. |
| R1138-B2-8 | OEIS and the Python standard-library documentation are selected through the trusted-source registry as declared sources with pinned extractors, endpoints, licenses, and content-addressed caches. | Implemented as declared trusted sources in `data/seed/sources-registry.lino` (`oeis`, `python_docs`); verified by the replay pins `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/oeis.rs` and `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/python_docs.rs`. |

## Issue #1163 Internet as Formal Knowledge

Issue [#1163](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1163) (E128,
part of the #1183 umbrella) turns fetched web pages into formal knowledge: one
generic page formalizer maps any fetched resource to a `LinkNetwork` (headings,
paragraphs, lists, tables, and language-tagged code blocks), search becomes the
entry point for a need no registered source covers, pages carry a data-driven
trust score and a rediscovery record, and queries over formalized pages answer
with links. The issue numbers its requirements 1 to 10; they are
`R1163-1` to `R1163-10` here in the same order. `R1163-11` to `R1163-16` are
the further obligations its "What to build", "How to test", "Design" and
"Definition of done" sections state without a number. The timeline, root
causes and prior art live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1163/`.

The module is `rust/src/web_formalize.rs` (with `rust/src/web_formalize_trust.rs`
included from it), not the `rust/src/page_formalizer.rs` the issue names; the
four test modules the issue sketches are consolidated in
`rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_web_formalize.rs`. The browser twin is
`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_web_formalize.js`, tested by
`rust/tests/web/issue-1163-web-formalize-parity.test.mjs`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1163-1 | A single `formalize_page(bytes, mime_hint) -> LinkNetwork` produces a `LinkNetwork` from any HTML, Markdown, plain-text, JSON, or PDF-text payload. | Implemented: `web_formalize::formalize_page` resolves the mime kind from the hint or the seed's sniff rules (`data/seed/page-formalization-rules.lino`) and builds a `page` root with one `heading` / `paragraph` / `list_item` / `table_row` / `code_block` child per block. Pinned by `html_page_formalizes_structure_and_code`, `markdown_fences_tag_languages_with_unknown_fallback`, `generic_formalizer_covers_bespoke_statements` (JSON) and `plain_and_pdf_text_formalize` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_web_formalize.rs`. The HTML walker once stepped over the whole document (an `<html>` open tag jumped the cursor past `</html>`) and the rule loaders once read no records (they iterated the top level, which holds only the file wrapper); both are fixed on this branch and the HTML test fails if either returns. Note: the network is assembled by inserting links, not by `LinkNetwork::parse`, and bare source files take the plain-text path. |
| R1163-2 | Every code block carries a language tag from the fence annotation, the HTML class, or a heuristic; an unrecognized fence yields `unknown`, never an empty tag. | Implemented: `resolve_language` walks the seed's `tag_source` order (fence, `html_class` with the seed's `language-` and `highlight ` class prefixes, the latter reading GitHub-style `highlight-source-<x>`, shebang and URL-extension heuristic) and falls back to the seed's `unknown`. Pinned by `markdown_fences_tag_languages_with_unknown_fallback` (fences `rust` and `shell`, bare fence `unknown`), `scala_page_tags_language_through_class_prefix`, `html_page_formalizes_structure_and_code` and `heuristic_tier_tags_unannotated_fences` (shebang `python`, URL extension `rust`) in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_web_formalize.rs`, and in the browser twin by the fence, class and heuristic tests of `rust/tests/web/issue-1163-web-formalize-parity.test.mjs`. The Rust tests named here were drafted on 2026-10-07 without a local cargo run; CI is their first verification. Gap: an annotated fence the seed does not know (for example a made-up tag) passes through verbatim rather than becoming `unknown`, and the URL-extension tier matches a suffix anywhere in the URL (`.c` would match `.com`), so it relies on the seed's row order. |
| R1163-3 | For each of the six bespoke extractors, `formalize_page` on the same fixture bytes yields every statement the bespoke extractor yields (generic ⊇ bespoke). | Implemented on fixtures: `concept_lookup::extractor_statements` exposes what each of the six bespoke extractors yields (the four lexical readers through `read_glosses`, `oeis_sequence_v1` through the new `oeis::record_statements`, `python_docs_v1` through `python_docs::page_statements`, which now shares `page_definitions` with the index builder), and `generic_formalizer_covers_every_bespoke_extractor` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_formal_knowledge_paths.rs` pins each extractor's real output exactly on its own fixture under `rust/tests/fixtures/issue-1163/<extractor>/` and checks the generic network covers it; `wiktionary_entry_v1` keeps its earlier test. The HTML walker gained `<dt>` as a list item so a reference page's signature line is a statement (mirrored in the browser twin). The Rust tests named here were drafted on 2026-10-07 without a local cargo run; CI is their first verification; the JavaScript twins are verified locally by `rust/tests/web/issue-1163-formal-knowledge-paths.test.mjs` (5 tests). Gap: the five new fixtures are hand-trimmed payloads in each API's shape, not byte captures, and the bespoke Python reader inserts a space at every inline tag where the generic walker does not, so pages with inline markup inside a signature compare only modulo whitespace. |

## Issue #1166 The Request Formalized into Obligations

Issue [#1166](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1166) (E131)
replaces phrase matching with request formalization: an issue body parses
into an obligation graph whose nodes carry semantic kinds and anchored
literals, mentions of the same quoted literal collapse to one node (the
structural fix for the Kotlin doubled output of #1156), and nothing
underivable is silently discarded. The root-cause analysis lives in
`docs/case-studies/issue-1166/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1166-1 | An issue body parses into an `ObligationGraph`; every enumerated requirement produces an `ObligationNode` anchored to seed meanings/roles. | Implemented: `rust/src/intent_formalization/obligations.rs` (`formalize_request`) builds on `obligation_ledger::ObligationNode::build` — no new ledger type — and classifies clauses against `print_stdout`, `ci_workflow_request`, and the program-request roles. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs`. |
| R1166-2 | Two or more mentions of the same quoted literal produce exactly one output-literal node. | Implemented: `coreference_pass` merges by literal value across clauses; `two_identical_output_clauses_produce_one_node` proves three mentions (intro, "print exactly", Expected Output) yield one node and one value. JavaScript root (2026-10-07): `coreferencePass` and the new `uniqueOutputLiteral`/`literalFor` in `js/agentic/crate/intent_formalization_obligations.mjs` hold the same cases. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-obligation-routing.test.mjs`. |
| R1166-3 | The executor derives its plan from obligation nodes and reports undischargeable nodes with byte spans. | Implemented 2026-10-07 (this pull request; the JS root verified locally, the Rust root awaiting CI). The graph exposes `obligations_of_kind` and `gap_report` (node id + byte span + reason). The executor's CI-workflow decision comes from the graph: `ci_workflow::requested_in` delegates to `intent_formalization::request_demands(objective, ObligationKind::CiWorkflow)`, and its JS twin `requestedIn` (`js/agentic/ci_workflow.mjs`) reads the same clause nodes (`ci_workflow_demand_is_read_from_the_obligation_graph`, Rust and JS). The program executor's output operands come from the graph too: `program_contract::explicit_stdout` and its JS twin `explicitStdout` read `intent_formalization::bound_output_literals` (`js/agentic/crate/intent_formalization_obligations.mjs` `boundOutputLiterals`), which assigns every quoted segment to the enumerated obligation clause (`clauses_with_spans`) that contains it and binds it when its introduction inside that clause evidences the seed `print_stdout` meaning, each value once. The routing change this makes, pinned in both roots: a print verb in an earlier enumerated clause no longer binds a literal in a later one (`Print the greeting! Then "Hello"` binds nothing; the old reading bound `Hello` because `!` was not one of its breaks); every other shape binds as before. The graph's broader `OutputLiteral` classification is kept for reporting rather than binding, so it cannot widen which prompts get a program contract; a literal it demands that the binding does not carry is reported (R1166-4). The clause vocabularies (output verbs, code style, file naming, CI badge) moved out of code into the seed roles `output_obligation_verb`, `code_style_obligation`, `file_naming_obligation` and `ci_badge_obligation` (`data/seed/meanings-repository-workflow.lino`), which the JS port reads too. The JS ledger's `opensAClause` now reads a line break before trimming, as the Rust `opens_a_clause` has since #1166, so both roots enumerate the same clauses. Pinned by the shared fixture `rust/tests/fixtures/issue-1166/executor-gaps.json` (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_executor_gaps.rs`, `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-executor-gaps.test.mjs`) and `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs`. The parity corpus `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json` has no program-contract case and the browser runtime is the Rust worker, so the Rust/JS twin parity for this routing lives in that shared fixture instead. |
| R1166-4 | A completed run emits an obligation report for each undischargeable node; none is silently omitted. | Implemented 2026-10-07 (this pull request; the JS root verified locally, the Rust root awaiting CI). `intent_formalization::obligation_gap_lines` is the report: the `gap_report` lines (clauses no rule can read) followed by `ObligationGraph::unbound_output_report` (output literals the graph demands that the executor's binding does not carry, under the `output_literal_not_bound_by_executor` reason of the `unbound_output_literal` rule in `data/meta/obligation-evidence-contract.lino`), so a demanded value the program would not print is no longer omitted silently. `record_obligation_gaps` writes each line as an `obligation_gap` event from every executor that reads the graph: the program-contract executor (`coding::program_contract::answer`, used by the solver and the agentic planner) and the catalog `write_program` executor in `rust/src/solver.rs` whenever the request formalizes into work obligations or demands the CI workflow the agentic work-item executor attaches. The JS agentic root keeps no event log, so its executor `programContractAnswer` (used by `js/agentic/planner.mjs` and `js/agentic/general_execution.mjs`) carries the same lines as `obligation_gaps`; the catalog `write_program` arm is native-only there (documented in `general_execution.mjs`), so that emission has no JS twin. The browser worker (`js/worker/`) records the same events (2026-10-07, verified locally): its catalog `WriteProgram` tail (`solverWriteProgramEvents`, `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_solver_events.js`) appends `solverObligationGapEvents` between `legacy_intent` and `procedure_cache`, where the native branch records them, behind the same gate. The port is `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_obligations.js` (clause enumeration, the clause-level ledger tree with its one-level checkable split, `derive_expectation`, the seed-role classifier, coreference, `bound_output_literals`, `obligation_gap_lines`) and `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_obligation_plans.js` (the general-planner mode `derive_expectation` consults, never the plan itself). Its vocabulary is the seed lexicon; the two `data/meta` decisions the worker cannot fetch (the expectation rules of `obligation-evidence-contract.lino` and the approved `missing_operation_contract` strategy of `task-decomposition-strategies.lino`) are mirrored in the worker and held equal to the files by its test. The fixture's `catalogCases` pin six catalog requests, five carrying work or CI obligations (one with an unbound output literal) and one carrying none, in the worker (`rust/tests/web/issue-1166-worker-obligation-gaps.test.mjs`: exact events, order and position; it also holds the worker's lines, plan modes and checkable splits equal to the agentic root on every fixture prompt and fourteen plan-shaped prompts) and in the native solver (`catalog_requests_record_the_worker_gap_lines` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_executor_gaps.rs`, awaiting CI; it checks the exact lines and their presence in the run's Links Notation, not their order there). Still open: the worker port is a hand mirror, not the Rust-to-WASM path the worker line budget asks for, so it must be kept in step with the Rust module by these tests. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_executor_gaps.rs`, `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-executor-gaps.test.mjs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-worker-obligation-gaps.test.mjs`, which assert the same fixture lines (node ids, spans, reasons) in the native, agentic and worker roots. |
| R1166-5 | An underivable clause yields `ObligationExpectation::Underivable`, split or reported, never discarded. | Implemented and pinned: `unknown_requirement_clause_yields_underivable_node_not_panic` (the ledger's own expectation semantics; the classifier leaves such nodes unclassified). JavaScript root (2026-10-07): `underivable` and `gapReport` keep the clause with its span. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-obligation-routing.test.mjs`. |
| R1166-6 | A translated body (en/ru/hi/zh/es) yields the same graph modulo the language tag. | Implemented for the fixture family: `kotlin_issue_ru_yields_same_obligation_count_as_en` and `kotlin_issue_hi_zh_es_yield_same_graph_modulo_language_tag` over `rust/tests/fixtures/issue-1166/hello-world-kotlin-{en,ru,hi,zh,es}.txt`; classification reads the seed lexicon's multilingual lexemes only; since 2026-10-07 the style, naming, badge and output-verb vocabularies are seed roles (`data/seed/meanings-repository-workflow.lino`) rather than code-side tables. JavaScript root (2026-10-07): `obligationKinds` (declaration order, as the Rust `Ord`) over the same five fixtures. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-obligation-routing.test.mjs`. |
| R1166-7 | A paraphrased body produces an equivalent graph. | Implemented: `paraphrase_en_yields_same_obligation_count_as_canonical_en` over `hello-world-kotlin-paraphrase-en.txt`. JavaScript root (2026-10-07): the same paraphrase fixture. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-obligation-routing.test.mjs`. |
| R1166-8 | Routing decides by the formalized request, not the leading word. | Implemented for the terminal router: `leading_shell_command` in `rust/src/solver_terminal.rs` now consults `request_carries_work_obligations` — a quoted output literal plus an authoring clause (program, CI, style, naming, badge) is a sentence about building something, in any of the five languages, while `git status` and `echo "Hello, World!"` stay commands (`work_obligation_requests_are_not_terminal_commands`). JavaScript roots (2026-10-07): `requestCarriesWorkObligations` in the agentic port, and the browser worker's terminal router: `leadingShellCommand` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_wikipedia_and_shell_commands.js`) now returns no command when `obligationCarriesWork` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_obligations.js`, the gate the catalog arm already used, split out) finds work obligations — before this the worker treated `make kotlin app printing "Hello, World!" plus GitHub Actions workflow`, whose words all parse as arguments, as a `make` command line. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-obligation-routing.test.mjs`. |

## Issue #1172 Factual QA Subject-Verified Lookup

Issue [#1172](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1172) (E137,
part of the #1183 umbrella) reports that "What is the capital of Australia?"
was answered with "The capital of the United States is Washington, D.C." —
the alias "us" matched as a raw substring inside "a**us**tralia". A wrong
answer is worse than no answer. This shard pins the delivered word-boundary
fix (R1, R4, R10, R11 of the issue), the subject Q-id gate (R2), seeded
comparisons (R6), questions over prompt-supplied text (R7) and the shared
parity case (R1172-12), and records the open follow-ups (R3, R5, R8, R9 and
the live-data halves of R6/R7) honestly. The root-cause
analysis, the corrected issue-0127 rows, and
the evidence live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1172/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1172-1 | A subject alias or question keyword may match the normalized prompt only at word boundaries (tokenized comparison), never as a raw substring inside a longer word: "us" must not match inside "australia"; multi-word aliases ("united states") match as consecutive token sequences; CJK surfaces, which have no inter-word spaces, keep substring matching. | Implemented: `FactRecord::matches_normalized` (`rust/src/seed/facts.rs`) now gates every alias and keyword through the new associated `FactRecord::contains_word_sequence`, which tokenizes the phrase with the same `engine::normalize_prompt` the caller applied to the prompt and requires a consecutive token run — the same contract as `seed::meanings::surface_present` (issue #386), mirrored for the fact store's own matching path. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1172_factual_qa_subject_match.rs`. |
| R1172-2 | A fact record may answer only when the formalized question's subject (Wikidata Q-id) equals the record's `subject_qid`; alias/keyword matching is retired as the primary mechanism. | Implemented (JavaScript verified locally; the Rust twin is drafted and awaits CI, no local `cargo` run): the subject gate. The question's subject is formalized — the browser worker's `parseFactQuestion` slot, the native `formalize_prompt_candidates` subject anchor when it is already a Wikidata item, otherwise the clause of the prompt that carries the asked `fact_relation` — and resolved to one Q-id through the fact store's own label index (aliases and localized subject labels mapped to `subject_qid`; the longest whole-word label wins, a tie between different Q-ids resolves to nothing).
