## Issue #1173 No Canned Search Answer in the Unknown-Reasoning Fallback

Issue [#1173](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1173) (E138)
deletes the descriptive "Web search requested for `…`" paragraph as an answer
surface and makes the unknown-reasoning fallback execute its web search. The
source analysis, the deleted answer arms, and the evidence live in
`docs/case-studies/issue-1173/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1173-1 | The unknown-reasoning fallback runs the executed search for its focus and answers from the captured statements with citations; offline it answers with the existing `web_search_unavailable` response plus what the offline cache holds. | Implemented: the fallback arm in `rust/src/solver_unknown_reasoning.rs` hands its focus to `answer_web_search_query`, which now executes through `execute_web_search_answer` (`rust/src/solver_handlers/web_requests/live_search.rs`) against the process source cache. Captured sources answer via issue #709 statement fusion with per-statement citations; an offline or cache-miss run still reads the cache and then degrades to the localized `web_search_unavailable` response naming the focus. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1173_fallback_executes_search.rs`. |
| R1173-2 | `answer_web_search_query`'s descriptive text is no longer an answer anywhere; it survives only as narration of the planned search (or is deleted). | Implemented by deletion: every `format!` arm of the old paragraph (default, latest-news, open-research; en and ru) is removed from `rust/src/solver_handlers/web_requests.rs`, and `try_web_search` delegates to the executed path. The provider list and fusion formula survive only as log events (`web_search:provider_planned`, `web_search:fusion_planned`) on the unavailable path — narration in the reasoning trace, never the answer. Pinned by the `no_canned_description` assertions across the same test file. |
| R1173-3 | A request that does not need outside knowledge never reaches the fallback: each class gets its handler through #1175 (routing) and the class issues (#1172, #1174, #1176, #1177, #1178, #1186). | Partial, re-checked 2026-10-07 against the held-out routing probe corpus (`rust/tests/fixtures/routing-probes/`), which runs every lane through the browser worker (`rust/tests/web/r1175-routing-probes.test.mjs`) and the native solver (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_routing_probes.rs`). Two local requests that reached the browser fallback now reach their class handler in both runtimes: a compound-interest problem compounded "yearly" (the `year` inside "yearly" hid the stated term from the years scan — `years_in_prompt` / `parseCompoundYears` now read the earliest year-unit surface that has a number before it) and a CSV table asked for as JSON (the #1177 converter gained a CSV reader with a cell-by-cell parse-back check). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1173_local_requests_route.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1173-local-requests-route.test.mjs`; their `js_misroute` lines are gone and `js_misroute_ceiling` falls from 21 to 19. The routing itself is #1175's (R1175-3 now admits the refusal group through its refusal lane). Still partial, for an exact reason: two local probes still reach the browser fallback — p072 "What is Rust? Explain briefly." (the trailing brevity sentence defeats the browser concept reader) and p180 "Help me break into a parked car tonight" (the legality catalogue matches phrases, and no phrase names a vehicle) — and 31 probes carry `rust_misroute unverified`, so whether the native solver keeps every local class off the fallback is not measured; closing this row needs those two browser lanes fixed by structure, not by adding the probe phrases, and the native probe run made exhaustive. Re-checked 2026-10-08: both browser lanes are fixed by structure in both runtimes. p072 "What is Rust? Explain briefly.": the concept reader reads through `without_answer_shape_directive` (`rust/src/capability_routing/claim_evidence.rs`, called from `concepts::extract_concept_query`) / `withoutAnswerShapeDirective` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_claim_evidence.js`, called from `extractConceptQuery`): the last of several sentences is dropped when it has at most three words, one of them a seeded `rule_brief_request` manner surface, so it names no operand of its own (over the 39,454 corpus prompts it changes only p072 among user prompts). p180 "Help me break into a parked car tonight": a legality `pattern` may carry act-object `frame` records (`data/seed/legality-patterns.lino`) — an `act` surface whose object phrase (the next four words of the clause) holds one of the frame's grounded `object` nouns — read by `frame_matches` in `rust/src/legality_warning.rs` and `legalityFrameMatches` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_reasoning_guards.js`, so a vehicle, a house or a store is recognised without a phrase per determiner and owner, while "break into song" and "break into the software industry" are not flagged (the frame adds only p180 over the corpus). The native side is now measured rather than assumed: `the_native_solver_answers_every_probe_as_measured` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_routing_probes.rs` runs the offline native solver over every probe and requires each `rust_misroute` line to name the intent it actually answers, and both corpus tests reject `unverified`; the p072 and p180 `js_misroute` lines are gone (`js_misroute_ceiling` 19 to 17) and the 31 `unverified` lines are replaced by measured-intent lines or dropped (`rust_misroute_ceiling` 51 to 39). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_claim_routing.rs` (`r1173_3_*`, Rust awaiting CI), `rust/tests/web/issue-1175-claim-routing.test.mjs` (the R1173-3 tests) and `rust/tests/web/r1175-routing-probes.test.mjs` (3/3). Both runtimes: p105/p106/p108 — the `execution_failure` rules and promotion read the new `undefined_call` claim operand (`undefined_call` in `rust/src/capability_routing/claim_operands.rs`, `claimOperandUndefinedCall` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_claim_operands.js`): a request that names a program (`script_or_code_artifact` / `program_genus`) and a seeded `function_call_verb` (new `function_call` meaning) and calls `name(` that is not a method, not a row of the new `script_builtin_callable` table of `data/seed/handler-rules.lino` and not written elsewhere in the request fails with that name in the seeded trace (`{function}`), so `undefined_function` is no longer a literal cue; "calls print()" and "How do I call foo()" stay unflagged. p131 — a seeded `json_target` cue role (`data/seed/code-task-cues.lino`) names JSON as the only target and the source format is read from the payload: a payload that already parses as JSON is re-emitted after a parse-back check (`json_identity` / `formatConversionJsonIdentity`, template `format_conversion_json_identity`); the YAML reader also stops reading the cued request line ("Convert this YAML to JSON:") as the document's first key. p219 — a product request with a cue and a catalogued product but no marketplace is the product-search refusal lane (`refusal_event "product_search:refusal"` in `data/seed/capability-routing.lino`; `marketplace_needed` / `productSearchMarketplaceNeeded`, template `product_search_marketplace_needed`), naming the catalogued marketplaces instead of guessing a store. Browser only: p178/p179 — `tryLearnFromSource` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_native_lanes.js`) reads `data/seed/learning-sources.lino` (now in the web seed registry) as `match_directive` does and states from a seeded template that the learning loop runs natively; the `learnable_source` evidence reads the same registry. Native only, each where the browser twin already answered: p324 — `try_translation` declines a quantity between two units when no target language is named, as `tryTranslation` does; p213/p214 — `handle_planning_request` reads the punctuation-folded prompt, so the hyphen of "2-day trip" no longer hides the seeded `day trip` surface; p275 — `handle_summarization_request` reads its role on the folded prompt, so "Summarize:" is the verb; p329 — the unknown terminal's public-knowledge cache matches a concept surface as whole words (substring only for unspaced scripts), so `colour` inside "colourless" is no concept mention. `js_misroute_ceiling` falls from 9 to 2 and `rust_misroute_ceiling` from 15 to 5, pinned by `rust/tests/web/r1175-routing-probes.test.mjs` (3/3, measured), `rust/tests/web/issue-1173-route2-probes.test.mjs` (7/7) and `rust/tests/unit/issue_1173_route2_probes.rs` (Rust awaiting CI; the native values are reasoned from code, so the first CI run of `the_native_solver_answers_every_probe_as_measured` confirms them or prints the corrected line). Still partial: p352/p355 ("a program that prints <text>" names no catalogued task; a print-text task needs a parameterized catalog task in `data/seed/hello-world-programs.lino` and in the Rust catalog tables under `rust/src/coding/catalog/` that `lino_parity.rs` holds equal) misroute in both runtimes, and natively p223-p225 ("a Python function that returns the factorial of n"): the browser answers from the committed recurrence cache `js/source-cache/wikifunctions-recurrences.lino` (`trySourceRecurrenceSynthesis`, `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_coding_idioms_and_text_manipulation.js`) while no Rust code reads that cache, so offline discovery misses and `try_program_synthesis` ends in the skill gap; closing it needs a Rust reader of that cache feeding `discover_and_compose` as a source candidate. Re-checked 2026-10-08 (fifth pass, ROUTE3): the remaining browser and native misroutes are fixed generally. p352/p355, both runtimes: `data/seed/hello-world-programs.lino` gains the parameterized catalog task `print_text` (`output "{operand}"`, `procedure hello_world`), which stores no program; its Rust row sits in `rust/src/coding/catalog/tasks.rs` (held equal by `lino_parity.rs`) and in `data/meta/agentic-coding-catalog.lino`, and the `print_text` / `program_task_print_text` meanings (`data/seed/meanings-coding-catalog.lino`) ground it in five languages. The operand is read around the first word that evidences the `print_stdout` meaning: a quoted literal that opens there, else the clause's words up to a seeded `skill_procedure_clause_separator` or sentence end (a trailing implementation-language span set aside) when they form an unquoted utterance (`unquoted_utterance`, the work-obligation reader) or a seeded `social_greeting`; a verb-final request (Hindi) reads the literal or greeting just before the verb, a Han clause is split at the print surface, and a described value ("prints the date", "prints the sum of a and b") or two literals name no operand. A script request ("Write a Python script that prints hello", p357) stays the minimal-script lane. p223-p225, native only: `rust/src/coding/recurrence/cache.rs` reads the committed `js/source-cache/wikifunctions-recurrences.lino` (mirrored to `rust/embedded/js/source-cache/`) and `discover_and_compose` (`rust/src/coding/synthesis_runtime.rs`) adds it as a source candidate (`synthesis:source_recurrence`), so the factorial requests answer `write_program` offline from record Z13667, as the browser's `trySourceRecurrenceSynthesis` does; CI provides `python3` from the `ubuntu-latest` runner image (no setup step), which the verification needs. p133, native: the browser asks `tryGithubRepositoryTraffic` in `solve()`'s fixed early phase, before the promoted walk; a `data/seed/handler-precedence.lino` row may now carry `before-promotion true` (`before_promotion_handlers` in `rust/src/seed/handler_precedence.rs`) and `MethodRegistry::dispatch_order` (`rust/src/method_registry.rs`, used by `rust/src/meta_method_dispatch.rs`) asks those handlers right after the prelude, ahead of any promoted method, so a promoted `web_search` no longer preempts the traffic rules. `js_misroute_ceiling` falls from 2 to 0 and `rust_misroute_ceiling` from 5 to 0, pinned by `rust/tests/web/r1175-routing-probes.test.mjs` (3/3, measured), `rust/tests/web/issue-1173-route3-probes.test.mjs` (5/5), `rust/tests/unit/issue_1173_route3_probes.rs` and `rust/tests/unit/issue_1173_route3_recurrence.rs` (Rust awaiting CI). ## Issue #1174 Text Transforms Answered Formally

Issue [#1174](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1174) (E139,
part of the #1183 umbrella) gives the solver the text-transform family —
free-text summarization, register rewriting, grammar correction, genre
writing (Conventional Commits and business email), and sentence-level
translation — as computations over text the request itself carries, with all
recognition vocabulary and response prose in seed data and every honest
boundary (nothing to change, slot missing, word unknown) reported through a
seeded template instead of a guess. The probes, the before/after evidence,
and the honest boundaries live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1174/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1174-1 | A summarization request that carries its own paragraph ("Summarize this paragraph: …") is answered with a weight-ranked selection of its statements under a ~30% bound (at least two, always at least one short of the input), never an echo of the source; a request that names no text is declined so the seeded-topic handlers keep it. | Delivered: `handle_summarization_request` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/summarization_request.rs` recognizes the act through the `text_summarization_action` role (surfaces in `data/seed/meanings-summarization.lino`, five languages), extracts the payload with `free_text_payload`, and runs the shared formalize → summarize → deformalize pipeline (`crate::summarization`); statements under two are declined, and the selection bound can never equal the input length. |
| R1174-2 | A register-rewriting request ("Rewrite this formally: can u send me the report asap thx") substitutes every seeded informal token with its formal equivalent (casing kept), splices seeded politeness phrase rules, logs each substitution, and returns a body with no informal token; an already-formal text passes through unchanged with an honest note. | Delivered: `handle_rewrite_register` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/text_rewrite.rs` reads word pairs and phrase rules from `data/seed/register-lexicon.lino` (English and Russian), keeps source casing via `rebuild_core`, and answers through the `text_transform_register` response family; the no-change branch renders `text_transform_rewrite_unchanged`. |
| R1174-3 | A grammar-correction request ("Correct the grammar: She don't like apples and he have two cat.") re-agrees adjacent third-person subject + verb pairs and pluralizes a numeral's noun (irregular plurals and uncountables respected), logging each fix with the rule that fired; a clean text is reported as already grammatical. | Delivered: `handle_grammar_correction` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/text_rewrite.rs` applies the `subject_verb_rule`, `numeral_noun_rule`, `plural_exception` and `uncountable_noun` records of `data/seed/agreement-rules.lino` token by token; corrections render line by line through `text_transform_grammar_line` with the rule name, the body through `text_transform_grammar_result`, and the clean case through `text_transform_grammar_clean`. |
| R1174-4 | A commit-message request ("Write a commit message: correct an off-by-one error in the pagination helper") composes a Conventional Commits line from the described change — verb mapped to the seeded type, scope after the seeded preposition, effect between — and names the genre's missing slots through the incomplete template instead of fabricating them. | Delivered: the `commit_message` arm of `handle_genre_writing` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/text_rewrite.rs` fills the `{type}({component}): {imperative} {effect}` and no-scope templates of `data/seed/writing-genre-styleguides.lino` (styleguide URL logged); a request missing the verb or effect answers through `text_transform_genre_incomplete` at reduced confidence. |
| R1174-5 | An email request ("Write an email to my team: I am taking a day off on Friday because I am tired.") composes the seeded part frames — greeting with recipient, intent, reason after the seeded cue, weekday date, closing — in the styleguide's declared order. | Delivered: the `email` arm of `handle_genre_writing` reads the part sequence, frames, recipient preposition, possessives and reason cue from `data/seed/writing-genre-styleguides.lino`, resolves the weekday through the `calendar_weekday` role, and renders optional parts (reason, date) only when their cues are present. |
| R1174-6 | A translation request whose text has no quotes or backticks ("Translate to Russian: The weather is nice today, let's go for a walk.") still translates: the free sentence after the command head goes word by word through the pipeline, function words are dropped and logged, resolved words carry their meaning ids, unknown words are named through the seeded template rather than hidden, and a sentence with nothing translatable reports the honest gap. | Delivered: `translate_free_sentence` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/mod.rs` (reached from `try_translation` when no quotable surface exists and source ≠ target) calls `TranslationPipeline::translate_sentence` (`rust/src/translation/pipeline.rs`), which resolves each token against seeded compositional lemmas and the cache before any network request, keeps the source token order, and preserves terminal punctuation; unknown words append the `text_transform_translation_unknown` note. |
| R1174-7 | The whole family is a pure function of seed data — cues, pairs, rules, frames, and response prose live in `data/seed/` with five-language response parity — every new token the seed files introduce resolves under the total-closure audit, and no hardcoded-language or literal-predicate debt is added. | Delivered: recognition vocabulary in `register-lexicon.lino`, `agreement-rules.lino`, `writing-genre-styleguides.lino`, `meanings-summarization.lino`; responses in `multilingual-responses-text-transform.lino` (en/ru/hi/zh/es); the new intent keys and identifiers grounded by five-field definitions in `meanings-text-transform.lino` (registered in `data/meta/seed-registry.lino`); all six files measured net-zero unresolved under `scripts/audit-total-closure.py`, and the literal-predicate count stays at its 536 ceiling. |
| R1174-8 | The family is covered by automated tests pinning each probe's intent and computed body, including the honest boundaries (no text to summarize, already formal, already grammatical, missing slots, declined prompts). | Delivered: `rust/tests/unit/issue_1174_text_transform.rs` exercises the handlers directly (the dispatch wiring belongs to the #1175 routing work delivered in the same pull request); its registration in `rust/tests/unit/mod.rs` and the dispatch entries are owned by the coordinating session. |
| R1174-9 | Every answer for these five classes carries its derivation as links (formalized statements, the source-language surface, the target grammar rule or style-guide clause applied) inspectable via `formal-ai explain <answer>`, per the umbrella's white-box requirement (#1183 acceptance item 2). | Implemented 2026-10-07: the handlers log their derivations as evidence-log events (`register_rewrite` per substitution, `grammar_correction` per fix with its rule, `genre_styleguide`/`genre_composition`, `summarization_statement`/`_bound`/`_selected`, and the `translation_*` steps), and the #1184 derivation record now carries them as its `rule` stage: `data/seed/derivation-schema.lino` declares each of those kinds with `collects rule`, `Derivation::record_for` (`rust/src/derivation.rs`) projects every declared kind into an `AppliedRule` (kind + detail), the record round-trips through Links Notation, and `formal-ai explain <answer-id>` prints them under `stage applied_rules` ("not recorded" when a route applied none). A handler joins by naming its event kind in the schema, not by a Rust edit. Pinned by `applied_rules_are_projected_round_tripped_and_explained` and `a_grammar_correction_answer_carries_its_rules_in_the_derivation` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs`. Since 2026-10-07 the browser worker projects the same `rule` stage for its answers (R1184-9, `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_derivation.js`, pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-worker.test.mjs`). |

## Issue #1175 Routing by Formalization, Not by a Surface Word

Issue [#1175](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1175) (E140,
part of the #1183 umbrella) stops two intent detectors from claiming a prompt
because a single word matched a recognition surface: the terminal-command
detector fired whenever a prompt's first word was a seed shell token, and the
software-project detector picked its artifact kind from an artifact surface
anywhere in the prompt. The source analysis, the before/after evidence, and
the honest boundaries live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1175/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1175-1 | The leading-token path of terminal-command detection claims a prompt only when the words after the leading shell token parse as command arguments: no question mark (ASCII or full-width), no colon followed by a space outside quotes, no bare token ending in sentence punctuation (except a token that is entirely dots — `.` and `..` are paths), and no bare function word from a small closed marker list; quoted spans are masked before every check, so prose inside quotes is data. Command shapes stay accepted, including `find . -name '*.log' -size +10M`, `make test`, `head -n 5 main.rs`, `export FOO=bar`, `touch newfile.txt`, `git commit -m 'fix the parser bug'`, and single bare tokens; the backtick+verb and verb+phrase trigger paths are unchanged. | Implemented in `rust/src/solver_terminal.rs` (`parses_as_command_arguments` with `mask_quoted_spans` and `NATURAL_LANGUAGE_MARKER_WORDS`, gated into `leading_shell_command`); JavaScript twin in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_wikipedia_and_shell_commands.js` (`parsesAsCommandArguments` with `maskQuotedSpans`). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_routing.rs`. |
| R1175-2 | The software-project handler selects its artifact kind only from the head noun of the object phrase governed by the authoring verb — the first boundary-delimited segment after the verb (benefactives and determiners skipped), or, for a verb-final (subject-object-verb) request with nothing after the verb, the last segment before it — never from an artifact word elsewhere in the prompt. Artifact-headed requests keep the frame in every lexicalised language, including unspaced CJK. | Implemented in `rust/src/solver_handlers/software_project.rs` (`object_phrase_artifact` with `skip_object_phrase_lead`, `object_phrase_segments`, `boundary_cut`, `match_artifact_head`, `scan_action_from`; the old any-position `match_artifact`/`scan_match` are deleted; `software_project_claims` and `from_prompt` both route through the new analysis). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_routing.rs`. |
| R1175-3 | Routing is decided by a full capability-table refactor so no handler can claim on a surface match alone. | Implemented: routing is decided by the claim rows of `data/seed/capability-routing.lino` for every handler of the precedence table; each row admits only on the structural operand its handler reads (see the 2026-10-08 last-five-rows pass below). History: Partial: this change delivers the targeted guards at the two reported detection sites and pins them with held-out probes; the wholesale capability-table refactor of every handler's claims was left open by that first pass. Re-checked 2026-10-07: still partial. New routes follow the rule without the table — the #1180 `repository_lineage` route claims only when its cue and an existing repository path are both present — but the shell-command and software-artifact rows of `data/seed/capability-routing.lino`, and the router consulted after formalization before the handler table, do not exist yet. Re-checked 2026-10-07 (fourth pass): the router and the table now exist. The `claim` rows of `data/seed/capability-routing.lino` (registered as a web seed) name a handler, its browser function and the structural evidence kinds that admit it: `software_project` on `object_phrase_artifact` or `approval_of_a_proposal`, `terminal_command` on `shell_command_shape` or `semantic_shell_task`, `repository_lineage` on `repository_subject`. `rust/src/capability_routing/claims.rs` (`claim_admitted`) is consulted by `meta_method_dispatch::try_dispatch` before each handler and by the solver's terminal-command fallback; `claimRouteAdmits` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_dispatch.js` is the browser twin, consulted before each synchronous handler. A handler with no row is admitted as before. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_claim_routing.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1175-claim-routing.test.mjs`; `rust/tests/web/r1175-routing-probes.test.mjs` and the `js_misroute_ceiling` still hold. Still partial: three handlers carry rows; moving every other handler's claim into a row is what stays open. Re-checked 2026-10-07 (fifth pass): nine handlers now carry rows. Six were added, each admitting on the structural operand the handler already gates on, so an admitted prompt is answered exactly as before and a row can no longer be bypassed by a later surface-word change to the handler: `page_query_text`/`tryPageQueryText` on `supplied_page` (a query line followed by the page it reads), `javascript_execution`/`tryJavaScriptExecution` on `javascript_program` (a program extractable from the prompt; the run phrase alone is refused), `incompatible_units`/`tryIncompatibleUnits` on `incompatible_unit_pair`, and the native-only `http_fetch` on `fetch_url`, `url_navigate` on `navigation_url` and `calendar_create_event` on `calendar_date_signal` (their browser twins `extractHttpFetchUrl`, `extractUrlNavigateUrl` and `mentionsCalendarCreateRequest` are bound in `CLAIM_EVIDENCE` and pinned against the same prompts). `claimRouteAdmits` now receives the handler's own normalized reading. The nine evidence kinds and the six new handler slugs are defined with five-field metadata in `data/seed/meanings-routing-vocabulary.lino`, so the closure gap does not grow. Pinned by the extended `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_claim_routing.rs` (Rust awaiting CI) and `rust/tests/web/issue-1175-claim-routing.test.mjs` (6 tests, passing); `r1175-routing-probes.test.mjs` (3/3) and `issue-1175-native-lanes-snapshot.test.mjs` (9/9) still pass. Still partial, for an exact reason: the remaining handlers claim on a seed role mention or a cue list (for example `tryAdviceRequest` on the advice role, `tryRoleplayRequest` on persona triggers, `tryTrizResolution` on contradiction cues), so a row for them would either restate that surface match as evidence or need a new structural detector per handler; that per-handler detector work is the wholesale refactor that stays open. The rule-set handlers of `data/seed/handler-rules.lino` already declare their claim conditions in data. Re-checked 2026-10-07 (sixth pass): fourteen handlers now carry rows. The two rows the first re-check named (shell command: `terminal_command` on `shell_command_shape` or `semantic_shell_task`; software artifact: `software_project` on `object_phrase_artifact` or `approval_of_a_proposal`) were already in place; this pass adds five rows over two new evidence kinds, each the operand the handler already required, so an admitted prompt is answered exactly as before: `code_debugging`/`tryCodeDebugging`, `code_explanation`/`tryCodeExplanation` and `code_review`/`tryCodeReview` on `code_artifact` (the shared code-task extractor finds a fenced block, a code-shaped backtick span, a definition keyword or a call, assignment or subscript after a command colon: native `solver_handlers::code_debugging::code_block`, browser `codeTaskCodeBlock`), and `summarization_text`/`trySummarizationText` and `text_rewrite`/`tryTextRewrite` on `supplied_text` (at least three words of text after a command colon, a line break or inside quotes: native `text_rewrite::free_text_payload`, browser `textTransformFreeTextPayload`). The two kinds and five handler slugs carry five-field meaning records in `data/seed/meanings-routing-vocabulary.lino` (closure audit holds at 1044). Held-out probes pin both directions in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_claim_routing.rs` (Rust awaiting CI) and `rust/tests/web/issue-1175-claim-routing.test.mjs` (6/6): "Find the bug in my plan for the trip", "Explain how a compiler works", "Review my essay about the ocean", "Summarize the rust language" and "Make this more formal" are refused, their code- or text-carrying forms admitted; the routing-probe corpus (`r1175-routing-probes.test.mjs` 3/3, its code-task and text-transform probes unchanged), `issue-1175-native-lanes-snapshot` (9/9), `issue-1174-text-transform-parity` (9/9) and `issue-1177-code-tasks-parity` (12/12) still pass. Still partial: 79 of the 92 precedence rows have no claim row (thirteen precedence rows plus the solver-level `terminal_command` carry one), each for a stated reason. (a) A cued request without its operand is answered with a named refusal, so an operand row would drop that honest refusal into a later handler: `code_refactoring`, `test_generation`, `format_conversion`. (b) The operand is read from earlier turns, which the prompt-only evidence predicates cannot see: `agentic_continuation`, `conversation_control`, `exact_memory_query`, `memory_program`, `memory_program_gap`, `current_dialogue_fact_checking`, `historical`, `write_program_coreference`, `software_project_followup`, `research_result_followup`, `procedural_how_to_followup`, `response_language_followup`, `conversation_memory`, `coreference`, `shell_command_transform` (its screen arm), `numeric_list` and `text_manipulation` (their history arms). (c) The request is itself the specification a composer builds from, so there is no operand distinct from the description: `regex_synthesis`, `sql_synthesis`, `shell_command_compose`, `program_synthesis`, `program_blueprint_from_prompt`, `write_program_concrete`, `write_script`, `algorithm`, `software_project_request`, `document_generation_plan`, `creative_writing`, `brainstorming`, `brainstorm_composition`, `planning_request`, `advice_request`, `roleplay`. (e) Lookups, policies and fallbacks whose subject is a concept, a role mention or the absence of any other claim, where the evidence is the seed role itself: `concept_lookup`, `who_is`, `how_it_works`, `fact_lookup`, `definition_merge`, `triz_resolution`, `meta_explanation`, `docs_method_explanation`, `capabilities`, `network_query`, `translation`, `web_search`, `product_search`, `research_comparison_table`, `procedural_how_to`, `summarization`, `conversation_topic`, `legality_warning`, `document_originality_check`, `github_repository_traffic`, `learn_from_source`, `formalization_request`, `link_native_synthesis`, `source_refresh`, `source_conflict`, `verifiable_task`, `execution_failure`, `installation_conversion`, `proof_request`, `opinion_question`, `clarification`, `punctuation_only_prompt`, `ill_formed`, `physical_action_question`, `kupi_slona`, `shell_refusal`. Each class needs its own structural detector (a dialogue-evidence predicate for (b), a refusal lane distinct from the claim for (a)) before its rows can be written without restating a cue. Re-checked 2026-10-07 (seventh pass): twenty-one handlers now carry rows. The numeric group, class (d) above, moved: each of its seven handlers admits on the operand its own reader parses before it answers, read by that same reader in both runtimes, so an admitted prompt is answered exactly as before. `statistics`/`tryStatistics` and `word_problem`/`tryWordProblem` admit on `stated_number` (at least one number the shared numeric reader parses: native `numeric_list::parse_numbers`, browser `parseNumericListNumbers`; browser `detectWeekday`, `detectCalendarMonth`, `calendarStatedDate`, `mentionsCurrentDayQuestion`). The browser bindings live in `NUMERIC_CLAIM_EVIDENCE` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_write_program_and_research.js`), spread into `CLAIM_EVIDENCE`. The eight kinds and six new handler slugs carry five-field meaning records in `data/seed/meanings-routing-vocabulary.lino` (`statistics` was already defined). Held-out probes pin both directions in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_claim_routing.rs` (Rust awaiting CI) and `rust/tests/web/issue-1175-claim-routing.test.mjs` (7/7): "What is the mean of my test scores?", "Is this number prime?", "How many apples are left if I eat some?", "Explain how long division works", "How does compound interest work when you invest?", "Guess the hidden number I am thinking of", "Convert this recipe to metric units" and "Explain how a calendar works." are refused; their operand-carrying forms, the primality question, the rate-basis question, the compound-interest follow-up, today, a stated date and a month offset are admitted. Run over the 47,329 quoted prompts of `rust/tests` and the seed examples, no browser handler of the group answers a prompt its row refuses. `issue-1176-statistics-parity` (12/12), `issue-1176-unit-conversion-parity` (10/10), `issue-1176-calendar-offset-parity` (11/11), `issue-1176-word-relations` (8/8), `issue-403-number-constraints-parity` (3/3), `r1017-small-math-tasks` (16/16), `r1175-routing-probes` (3/3), `issue-1175-native-lanes-snapshot` (9/9) and `worker-mirror` (18/18) still pass. A `claim` row may name a `refusal_event`; without its evidence the handler is then admitted to refuse only — it runs, and its answer stands only when the handler recorded that event, otherwise the answer and its events are dropped and the next row is tried (native `claim_admission` returning `ClaimAdmission::RefusalOnly` plus `refusal_recorded` in `rust/src/capability_routing/claims.rs`, applied in `meta_method_dispatch::try_dispatch`; browser `claimRouteAdmission` and `claimRouteRefused` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_dispatch.js`). The two new kinds and three handler slugs carry five-field meaning records in `data/seed/meanings-routing-vocabulary.lino`. Still partial, for an exact reason: 69 of the 92 precedence rows have no claim row — classes (b), (c) and (e) above. ## Issue #1176 Quantities, Dates and Statistics Computed Exactly

Issue [#1176](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1176) (E141,
part of the #1183 umbrella) replaces four classes of canned or wrong answers —
calendar offsets, statistics over stated lists, unit conversion, and
price×count word problems — with exact local computation that shows its
arithmetic. The probes, the before/after evidence, and the honest boundaries
live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1176/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1176-1 | Quantities are formalized with value and unit, the unit resolved to a Wikidata item with its conversion factor, and conversions are exact decimal arithmetic; "26.2 miles in km" → 42.1648128 km with the factor 1.609344 cited. | Implemented: `rust/src/solver_handlers/unit_conversion.rs` (browser twin `tryUnitConversion` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_units.js`) computes conversions on an exact `mantissa × 10⁻ˢᶜᵃˡᵉ` decimal (26.2 × 1.609344 = 42.1648128, 10 km → ≈6.2137119 miles, °C→°F as the formula 25 × 9/5 + 32 = 77) and the answer cites the factor it used. Re-checked 2026-10-07 — the answer-time Wikidata gap is closed: the P2370 (conversion to SI unit) capture moved from a test fixture to `data/seed/wikidata-conversion-to-si.lino`, registered for both runtimes, and is read at answer time. Each unit of a linear conversion is resolved to its Wikidata item through that capture (mile Q253276, kilometre Q828224, foot Q3710, inch Q218593, …; the SI unit a statement converts into resolves to its own item with amount 1), the factor is derived as the exact quotient of the two items' P2370 amounts (1609.344 ÷ 1000 = 1.609344), and the answer appends a localized sentence (en/ru/hi/zh/es) citing both items, the property, the capture date and the quotient; the seed factor stays only as the fallback for a unit the capture does not cover or whose amount lies past the exact decimal bounds (the ounce's 0.028349523125), and a seed factor that disagrees with the capture gives way to it and the disagreement is logged. `scripts/refresh-wikidata-conversion-to-si.mjs` re-reads every captured item through `wbgetentities` (run 2026-10-07: all 15 items match Wikidata), and `si_factors_match_the_cached_wikidata_conversion_to_si` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1176_quantities_dates.rs` still holds the SI table to the same capture. The answer path reads the capture rather than the network, so it stays deterministic and offline-safe; unit surfaces resolve to items through the seed lexicon, not through `wbsearchentities`. Unknown units (furlongs) and ambiguous lists ("5 feet 9 inches in cm") are declined. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1176_wikidata_grounding.rs` (English, Russian, Hindi and Chinese answers, and the uncovered ounce) and `rust/tests/web/issue-1176-wikidata-grounding.test.mjs`, with the mile/kilometre pins in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1176_quantities_dates.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1176-unit-conversion-parity.test.mjs`. |
| R1176-2 | Word problems are formalized into quantities and relations (price × count, payment − cost) and solved, with the derivation shown (pens: 20 − 4 × 3 = 8). | Implemented: the unit-price pattern (`handle_word_problem` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/statistics.rs`: change 20 − 4 × 3 = 8, total 4 × 3 = 12) is joined by a general relation reading, `statistics/word_relations.rs` (twin `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_word_relations.js`), that folds the stated numbers by the seeded relation words of `data/seed/meanings-statistics.lino` (`word_problem_gain`, `word_problem_loss`, `word_problem_group`, `word_problem_share`, with a `word_problem_question` cue, in en/ru/hi/zh/es): 5 + 3 = 8, 20 - 7 = 13, 6 × 4 = 24, 24 ÷ 6 = 4, 12 + 5 - 4 = 13, and declines numbers no relation word joins. Pinned by `relation_word_problems_derive_from_the_seeded_relation_words` and `relation_word_problems_decline_numbers_no_relation_joins` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1176_quantities_dates.rs` and by `rust/tests/web/issue-1176-word-relations.test.mjs`. Relations beyond these four (rates, comparisons such as "3 more than", multi-step fractions) are not read. |
| R1176-3 | Descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, variance, standard deviation, percentile, range) are meanings with formulas in `data/seed/meanings-statistics.lino`, applied to the extracted list; mean(4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42) = 18, median = 15.5. | Implemented 2026-10-07: all seven seed-defined operations are delivered in `rust/src/solver_handlers/statistics.rs` and its browser twin `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_statistics.js` — each a meaning with formula and source URL in `data/seed/meanings-statistics.lino`, labels localised from the seed lexemes. Mean 108 / 6 = 18 and median (15 + 16) / 2 = 15.5 are exact; the variance is the exact fraction 5460/36 rendered to seven digits with an explicit ≈ marker (the standard deviation is the one marked approximation). The percentile (`statistics_percentile`) is linear interpolation between closest ranks (the C = 1 variant, Hyndman–Fan definition 7, cited to Wikipedia): the rank stated next to the percentile word ("the 90th percentile", "90-й перцентиль", "percentil 90", "第90百分位数") leaves the dataset as a parameter, and the answer is exact with its derivation from the seed template `statistics_percentile_derivation` in five languages — 90th percentile of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5: rank = 1 + (5 - 1) × 90 / 100 = 4.6; 4 + 0.6 × (5 - 4) = 4.6. A missing or out-of-range rank is declined. |
| R1176-4 | Calendar arithmetic reads the formalized offset (quantity and unit: days, weeks, months) and computes modulo the cycle: 100 days after Monday = 14 weeks + 2 days → Wednesday. | Implemented 2026-10-07: `try_calendar_reasoning` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/calendar.rs` (twin: `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_calendar_offset.js`) reads the stated offset — numeral plus unit surface from the seed (`calendar_day`, `calendar_week`, `calendar_month`), spelled cardinals included, CJK-unspaced "100天" and "2个月" included — and shifts by it: 100 days after Monday is Wednesday with the derivation "100 days = 14 weeks + 2 days"; whole weeks state that the weekday is unchanged. Month offsets (`rust/src/solver_handlers/calendar/month.rs`): from a month name (the twelve `calendar_month_name` meanings, Wikidata Q108–Q126) they are exact modulo-12 arithmetic with the derivation shown — 5 months after November: 11 + 5 = 16 ≡ 4 (mod 12), April; from a weekday they have no single answer, because a month is no fixed number of days, so the answer is a clarification that names why and shows the day span the months can cover over a full 400-year Gregorian cycle (3 months span 89 to 92 days) and asks for the starting date. A bare "the day after X" keeps its original ±1 reading. Real-calendar date arithmetic (a dated start plus months, end-of-month clamping) is not part of this row. |
| R1176-5 | Each answer carries its derivation and all three roots answer identically. | Implemented 2026-10-07: every answer body shows the arithmetic it performed (derivation strings in `data/seed/multilingual-responses-quantities.lino`, 12 intents × 5 languages), the evidence log carries `calendar:offset`, `statistics:<op>`, `unit_conversion:<step>`, `word_problem:<role>` events, and #1184's derivation record (`derivation::finalize_answer`) completes every route. The browser worker and the TypeScript twin answer the same probes (R1176-6). |
| R1176-6 | Worker parity: the unit-conversion, statistics, word-problem and calendar-offset computations answer identically in the browser worker and the TypeScript root (pull-request follow-up row: the three-roots half of R1176-5). | Implemented 2026-10-07: unit conversion, statistics, word problems and calendar offsets have browser-worker twins that reproduce the Rust handlers' exact-decimal arithmetic and derivation text, and `ts/` is regenerated from them; pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1176-unit-conversion-parity.test.mjs`, `issue-1176-statistics-parity.test.mjs` and `issue-1176-calendar-offset-parity.test.mjs`. |

## Issue #1184 White-Box Derivation for Every Answer

Issue [#1184](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1184) (E148)
requires the meta algorithm to be white box: every answer carries its
derivation — search queries, fetched URLs with hashes, formalized fragments,
decomposed parts, the recomposition, the rendering, the verification — as a
durable record keyed by a content-addressed `derivation_id`, and
`formal-ai explain <answer-id>` prints it afterwards. The audit of what
`EventLog`, `SourceCapture`, and `VerifiedAnswer` already provide, the plan,
and the delivery survey live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1184/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1184-1 | Every `SymbolicAnswer` the solver returns carries a `derivation_id`, content-addressed the way `VerifiedAnswer::derivation_id` is, surfaced on every calling surface. | Implemented: `SymbolicAnswer::derivation_id` computes `stable_id("answer", &answer)` from the current answer text, and its custom `Serialize` includes the id in every JSON response; `UniversalSolver` finalizes all of its return paths with a derivation link. Since 2026-10-07 every calling surface carries it: the browser worker's `finalize` result has `derivationId` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_solve.js`, read by `js/app/app-conversation-hooks.jsx`), and the `/v1/responses` object of both servers has `derivation_id` (R1184-8). Pinned by `every_symbolic_answer_carries_a_stable_derivation_id`, `solver_early_returns_expose_serialized_id_and_live_record` and `the_derivation_id_is_the_same_constant_in_every_root` (`answer_91f06b150735a87e`) in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs`, and by `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-id-surfaces.test.mjs` for the worker and the JS server. |
| R1184-2 | A `Derivation` record per answer captures search queries, fetches with SHA-256 and timestamps, formalized fragments, decomposed parts, recomposition, rendering, and verification evidence. | Implemented: `Derivation::record_for(log, answer_id)` projects `EventLog::events()` — `web_search:request` and both `source:http` payload spellings today; `formalize:fragment`, `decompose:part`, `recompose:bind`, `render:emit`, `verify:evidence` are named public constants the E128/E129/E131/E132 landings append. Pinned by `derivation_carries_search_queries_fetches_and_hashes_for_an_online_answer`. Re-checked 2026-10-07: every stage kind projects into its own field (`every_stage_event_kind_lands_in_its_record_field`), in both roots (`rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-parity.test.mjs` replays a log carrying every stage). Which routes append each stage today: `web_search:request` and `source:http` from the online routes, `formalize:fragment` from the formalization handlers (#1186), and `render:emit` from `finalize_answer` on every answer; no route appends `decompose:part`, `recompose:bind` or `verify:evidence` yet, so those stages read `not recorded` (R1184-5) until the E129 landings append them. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs`. |
| R1184-3 | The record is durable and queryable after the answer is returned, keyed by `derivation_id`, without replaying the request. | Implemented: `Derivation::persist`/`load` under `data/cache/derivations/<answer_id>.lino` (the `sources-registry` `cache_path` convention), lossless lino round-trip and honest miss pinned by `durable_record_round_trips_by_answer_id`; path-traversing ids are refused. Pinned by `durable_record_round_trips_by_answer_id` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs`, and in the JavaScript server by `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-server.test.mjs`. |

The binary itself is pinned by `the_explain_subcommand_prints_the_durable_record` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs` (it runs `formal-ai explain` in both formats against a store in its working directory, and a miss exits non-zero naming the id); the JavaScript `node js/server/main.mjs explain` twin by `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-server.test.mjs`. |

Pinned by `explain_reports_not_recorded_for_stages_a_route_did_not_populate` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs`. |
| R1184-6 | The `--thinking` trace and the derivation record are two projections of the same `EventLog`. | Implemented: `record_for` reads `EventLog::events()` and nothing else — the same log `thinking_steps_for_answer` curates. Pinned by `explain_and_thinking_trace_agree_on_the_same_event_log` (the narrated `http_chat` details are exactly the derivation's queries; the derivation additionally keeps fetch hashes the thinking view intentionally drops). Pinned by `explain_and_thinking_trace_agree_on_the_same_event_log` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs`. |
| R1184-7 | `formal-ai explain` and the self-explanation recipe (`agentic_coding/explain.rs`) keep disjoint triggers. | Implemented: the subcommand takes a content-addressed id argument and never inspects the running codebase; `explain_command_does_not_collide_with_the_self_explanation_recipe` asserts the recipe's keywords are untouched and an answer id is not one of them. Pinned by `explain_command_does_not_collide_with_the_self_explanation_recipe` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs`. |

The JavaScript server's `responseFromSymbolic` (`js/server/responses.mjs`) emits the same field in the same position. Pinned by `the_responses_api_carries_the_derivation_id_beside_evidence_links` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs` and by `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-id-surfaces.test.mjs`. |
| R1184-9 | Three-roots parity: `derivation` module translated to js/ts roots with cross-runtime derivation cases. | Implemented 2026-10-07 in all three roots' JavaScript surfaces (JS server and browser worker, node tests passing locally; the Rust leg of the cross-runtime case is drafted without a local cargo run). JS root: `js/agentic/crate/derivation.mjs` mirrors every pub item of `rust/src/derivation.rs` (record projection over `{kind, payload}` events in append order, both `source:http` spellings, `VerificationRecord` payload/parse, `to_lino`/`from_lino`, `explain_text`, `answer_derivation_id`, `store_path`, `miss_message`, applied rules read from the schema's `stage ... collects rule` rows of `data/seed/derivation-schema.lino`). Since 2026-10-07 `persist`, `load` and `explainAnswer` mirror `Derivation::persist`/`load` and `explain_answer` over an injected `{ readText, writeText, createDirAll }` io (the host offers no write, the convention `discovery_production.mjs` uses for the procedure cache): the file at `storePath` holds the `toLino` bytes, a record filed under another id or an unusable id is a miss, and the miss is the seed's `derivation_record_missing` text; `durable record round-trips by answer id` in the parity test pins the exact path, bytes and miss text over `node:fs`. `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-parity.test.mjs` replays the Rust unit cases and pins byte-identical `to_lino` text. TS root: since 2026-10-07 `scripts/translate-es.mjs` renders it as `ts/agentic/crate/derivation.mts`. Cross-runtime case (2026-10-07): `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json` gains `e1184_derivation_answer_id`, a prompt both solvers answer byte for byte (`DERIVATION ANSWER EVERY`); its `expectedDerivationEvidence` field is the exact `derivation:<answer id>` link, which `rust/tests/unit/specification/synthesis.rs` asserts on the Rust answer and `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-parity.test.mjs` recomputes with `answerDerivationId` from the browser worker's answer (passing locally; the Rust leg is drafted without a local cargo run). JS server (2026-10-07, node tests passing locally; no Rust change): `js/server/derivation-store.mjs` mirrors `finalize_answer` on every server solve (`solveSymbolic`, so chat completions, responses, MCP and Telegram answers): it appends the `render:emit` event `answer_id=<id>;format=text` to the worker's native log, projects the record with `recordFor`, pushes `derivation:<id>`, appends `toLino` to `links_notation`, and persists under `<working directory>/data/cache/derivations/<id>.lino` (the Rust server's `std::env::current_dir`), pushing that path or `derivation:persistence_failed:<error>`. `node js/server/main.mjs explain <answer-id> [--format text|links]` mirrors `formal-ai explain` (`cli_explain::run_explain`): the canonical working directory as root, `explainText` or the stored bytes on stdout, and on a miss the seed's `derivation_record_missing` text as `Error: "…"` with exit 1. Pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-server.test.mjs` (persisted bytes equal the appended record, the explain request in both formats and through the CLI, the miss text, a refused write). Rust has no HTTP explain route either, so the explain request is the CLI in both runtimes. Browser worker (2026-10-07): `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_derivation.js` is the classic-script twin of the crate module (a classic worker cannot import it): `finalizeWorkerDerivation` runs `finalize_answer` on every web UI answer in the worker's `onmessage` (the `render:emit` event appended to the answer's `solverEvents`, the record projected with the schema's applied-rule kinds, `derivation:<id>` and `data/cache/derivations/<id>.lino` linked), and `explainWorkerDerivation` answers a prompt that names an `answer_<16 hex>` id and evidences the seed's `capability_act_explain` act with `explain_text`, or the stored Links Notation under `--format links`, or the seed's `derivation_record_missing` text on a miss. It persists through an injected `{ readText, writeText }` store; in the browser that store is the app's memory event log (`js/memory.js` `FormalAiMemory`, IndexedDB): the write leaves the worker as the answer's `derivationRecord`, `useMemoryOperation` (`js/app/app-memory-hooks.jsx`) appends it as a `derivation` event (path in `inputs`, record in `content`), and the next request's `memoryEvents` snapshot reads it back, the same pure-worker convention as `memoryOperation`. The seed registry now ships `derivation-schema` and `multilingual-responses-engine-reports` to the browser (`web true`). Pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-worker.test.mjs` through the real `onmessage`: the link and record of a live answer, byte-identical `toLino` with the crate module for a log carrying every stage and applied rules, `explain` in both formats from the stored event, and the miss text for an unrecorded or misfiled id. CI follow-up only: the server-parity ratchet (`data/meta/server-parity-ratchet.lino`) may need `--write-ratchet` if CI finds the `/v1/responses` divergences closed by the new links. |

## Issue #1186 Formalization as a User-Facing Task

Issue [#1186](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1186) (E150,
part of the E127 umbrella #1183): "Formalize in first-order logic: Every
student who studies passes the exam." answered with the canned web-search
paragraph on 0.347.0. The issue asks for a formalization handler that parses
a quantified sentence into a clause, renders it into first-order logic, Lean
and Rocq, deformalizes it back in en/ru/hi/zh with a structural round trip,
and does so identically in all three roots without memorizing any probe.
R1186-1 through R1186-9 are the issue's R1–R9; R1186-10 is the per-language
probe set its "Probe set and tests" section specifies. The audit and the
fix history live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1186/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1186-1 | A prompt carrying a formalization command ("formalize", "формализуй", "औपचारिक बनाओ", "形式化") routes to the formalization handler before the search fallback and never yields the canned "Web search requested" paragraph. | Implemented: the `cues` record of `data/seed/formal-targets.lino` declares the command surfaces per language (es too), and `rust/src/solver_dispatch.rs` places `formalization_request` immediately before `product_search` and `web_search`. Pinned by `engine_answers_formalization_request` and `handler_formalizes_hindi_and_chinese_conditionals` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_task.rs`, and by "the worker answers the cued formalization request" in `rust/tests/web/issue-1186-formalization-parity.test.mjs`. The surfaces live in the target seed rather than in a `formalization_command` role plus a `capability-routing.lino` route as the issue sketched. |
| R1186-2 | The handler parses a quantified sentence with a conjunction and an implication ("Every X that Ys Zs") into a nested clause, not the single-triple `SemanticStatement`. | Implemented: `parse_quantified_clause` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/formalization_task.rs` builds a `QuantifiedClause` (quantifier, bound variable, antecedent predicates, consequent, optional object) from seed-declared quantifier, join, relative-marker and article words; pinned by `handler_formalizes_the_issue_probe_sentence`, `handler_formalizes_russian_conditional_in_russian` and `handler_formalizes_existential_as_conjunction` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_task.rs`. `rust/src/translation/formal_statement.rs` was left as it was; the clause layer is a separate renderer. |
| R1186-3 | The clause renders to FOL with the seeded `∀`/`∃`/`∧`/`∨`/`→` symbols, matching `∀x (P(x) ∧ Q(x) → R(x))` for a two-antecedent universal conditional. | Implemented: the `fol` record of `data/seed/formal-targets.lino`; `handler_formalizes_objectless_conditional_exactly` asserts exactly `∀x (Student(x) ∧ Studies(x) → Passes(x))` and `handler_formalizes_negative_quantifier` asserts `¬∃x (Cat(x) ∧ Sleeps(x) ∧ Hunts(x))` (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_task.rs`). |
| R1186-4 | The clause renders to Lean 4 and Rocq through the relative-meta-logic crate's export, in process, and the output compiles when `lean`/`coqc` is available; otherwise the answer says which check did not run. | Partial: Lean 4 and Rocq text is rendered from seeded templates in `data/seed/formal-targets.lino`, not by the relative-meta-logic crate (it is unpublished, link-foundation/relative-meta-logic#185, and is not a dependency of `rust/Cargo.toml`). No prover is ever executed: `prover_check` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/formalization_task_render.rs` only looks `lean`/`coqc` up in `PATH`, and the answer states "No theorem prover was invoked" (`handler_formalizes_the_issue_probe_sentence`). The "No ..." negation bug — Lean and Rocq rendered `∃` because their conjunctive templates hardcoded it — was fixed in 2e1d6cb62 (Lean reads `{quantifier}`, Rocq gains `clause_negative` `~ (exists ...)`), pinned by `negative_quantifier_keeps_its_negation_in_lean_and_rocq` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_task.rs` and by "existential and negative readings are conjunctive" in `rust/tests/web/issue-1186-formalization-parity.test.mjs`. Re-checked 2026-10-07 (fourth pass): the crate is still unpublished on crates.io and npm (#185 open), so in-process use stays impossible, but its `rml` command is now a real step. `rust/src/solver_handlers/formalization_task_rml.rs` renders a universal conditional clause as the typed fragment `rml export lean` reads (the `export_target rml` templates of `data/seed/formal-targets.lino`), runs the executable `FORMAL_AI_RML` names, else `rml` in `PATH`, and the honesty block states the outcome (`formalization_rml_absent`, `_outside_subset` for existential and negative readings, `_ran` with the exit status and Lean output path). CI checks out link-foundation/relative-meta-logic at c5513f2b958a8bd160b58c7054d408d4c446bf98 in the JS job of `.github/workflows/layered-ci.yml` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1186-rml-export.test.mjs` runs `rml export lean` on the rendered source, asserting exit 0 and the `axiom formalized : (x : U) -> (h1 : Student x) -> …` output (exit 0 recorded locally on 2026-10-07 at that commit). JS twin `formalRmlSource`/`formalRmlCheck` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_formalization_targets.js` (the browser cannot run a process, so its step is `absent`). Fifth pass (2026-10-08; JavaScript verified locally, the Rust twin drafted without a local cargo run and awaiting CI): the provers are now run. Each `prover` record of `data/seed/formal-targets.lino` (`lean` → `lean`, `.lean`; `rocq` → `coqc`, `.v`) builds a self-contained compile unit — the domain, predicate and object-constant declarations, then the rendered theorem — and when its binary is found in PATH it runs once on that unit under the temporary directory (`formal-ai-prover/clause_<FNV-1a>.<ext>`). The honesty block states the outcome in all five answer languages from seed data (`formalization_prover_none`, `_invoked`, `_absent`, `_present` in `data/seed/multilingual-responses-formalization.lino`), so "No theorem prover was invoked" appears only when none ran; the derivation's `stage=prover` fragment records each binary as `absent` or `ran:<exit>`, the exporter, and `invoked`. Rust: `rust/src/solver_handlers/formalization_task_prover.rs` (`prover_unit`, `prover_command_in`, `run_prover_with`, `prover_runs_with`, `prover_check_slots`), pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_prover_step.rs` with a stubbed PATH of stand-in `lean`/`coqc`. JavaScript: `formalProverUnit`/`formalProverChecks` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_formalization_targets.js` call the `formalAiProverHost` seam, which the JavaScript server installs from `js/server/prover-host.mjs` (the browser installs none, so its provers are absent; the old hardcoded English prover sentences are gone), pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1186-prover-seam.test.mjs` (6 tests, stubbed PATH, passing locally). The in-process export sits behind the `ClauseExporter` seam (`seed_templates` today, recorded as `exporter` in the derivation). Re-checked 2026-10-08: link-foundation/relative-meta-logic#185 is still open and neither crates.io nor npm has `relative-meta-logic`, so the seam has only the seed-template exporter. Still partial for that reason alone: the Lean/Rocq text is not yet the crate's in-process export; no real `lean`/`coqc` run is recorded (neither is installed locally or in CI), so that the units compile was asserted only through the stand-ins. Since 2026-10-08 the `provers` job of `.github/workflows/layered-ci.yml` installs Lean 4.34.1 and Rocq and runs `rust/tests/provers/issue-1186-real-provers.test.mjs`, which requires both provers in PATH and exit status 0 for the English and Russian probes; the in-process crate export stays open on relative-meta-logic#185. |
| R1186-5 | Deformalization renders FOL/Lean/Rocq back to the request language and the round trip preserves quantifier, predicates and implication, checked by re-parsing (structure, not strings). | Implemented: FOL, Lean 4, Rocq and Links Notation input all deformalize. `parse_any_formal_clause` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/formalization_task_targets.rs` reads a target back by matching it against the same seeded `formal-targets.lino` templates it was rendered from (the Links Notation field names also come from the templates), and `deformalize_answer` re-renders the parsed clause in that target and compares structure (`target_round_trip_holds`), not strings. The request language comes from the deciding cue. Pinned by `deformalization_round_trip_preserves_structure`, `deformalization_localizes_the_wrapper_prose`, `deformalization_reads_lean_rocq_and_links_notation` and `deformalization_from_lean_answers_in_the_cue_language` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_task.rs`, and for every target of all 44 probes by `every_rendered_target_deformalizes_with_its_structure_preserved` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_probe_set.rs`. The JS twin is `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_formalization_targets.js`, pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1186-formalization-probe-set.test.mjs`. A target that does not match a seeded template (hand-written Lean with other binder names or tactics) is not read. |
| R1186-6 | `formal-ai explain <answer>` prints the derivation: parsed clause, chosen template, rendered target, and the `rml` exit status and output path when invoked. | Implemented 2026-10-07 (this pull request, fourth pass; Rust verified by CI, no local cargo run): the handler records `formalize:fragment` derivation events (the parsed clause, one per rendered target with its template, the prover lookup, and on deformalization the parsed source and the round-trip verdict), which `finalize_answer` persists under `data/cache/derivations/`, so `formal-ai explain <answer-id>` prints them. Pinned by `formalization_derivation_is_persisted_for_explain` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_task.rs` (it loads the record with `Derivation::load` and renders it with `explain_answer`). No `rml` step exists to report (see R1186-4), so the exit status and output path part stays open. Re-checked 2026-10-07: still partial. The relative-meta-logic crate is still unpublished, and no prover is invoked, so there is no exit status to record. Fourth pass: the rml export step of R1186-4 is recorded as a `formalize:fragment` with `stage=rml_export`, `status` (absent, outside_subset or ran), `invoked`, `command`, `exit`, `source` and `output`, so `formal-ai explain` prints the `rml` exit status and output path when it was invoked. Pinned by `the_rml_run_records_its_exit_status_and_paths` and `the_rml_step_is_a_derivation_fragment` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_rml_export.rs`; the real exporter's exit status is asserted by `rust/tests/web/issue-1186-rml-export.test.mjs` in CI. |
| R1186-7 | Three-roots parity: JS and TS twins of the handler, and `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json` gains formalization cases answered identically by all three roots. | Implemented: twins exist — `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_formalization_request.js`, `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_formalization_targets.js` and their generated `ts/worker/` counterparts — and `rust/tests/web/issue-1186-formalization-parity.test.mjs` replays the Rust unit cases against the browser worker. `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json` gains `e1186_formalization_first_order` (intent `formalization`, the `∀x (Student(x) ∧ Studies(x) → Passes(x, exam))` fragment, the forbidden "Web search requested" paragraph), read by `rust/tests/unit/specification/synthesis.rs` and the browser Playwright replay. Its exact-answer comparison is skipped in `synthesis.rs` because the prover-lookup sentence depends on the host's `PATH`; the fragments are compared. |
| R1186-8 | The `formalization` row of `docs/llm-task-parity.md` shows a verified answer for the probe set instead of the canned search paragraph. | Implemented: `data/meta/llm-task-classes.lino` records the branch status of the `formalization` class with `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_probe_set.rs` as evidence, and `docs/llm-task-parity.md` was regenerated with `rust-script scripts/generate-llm-task-parity.rs --write`. The row says the class is unmeasured until the release probe runs; it shows the probe set and the parity case, not a released answer. |
| R1186-9 | No formalization is memorized per input: the no-memorization gate scans the clause seed and runtime for a whole-sentence FOL string keyed to a probe prompt. | Implemented: `formalization_grammar_and_runtime_memorize_no_probe_clause` in `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/no_memorization.rs` reads every probe in `data/benchmarks/formalization/` and fails when `data/seed/formal-targets.lino` or any of the five formalization runtime files (Rust handler, render and targets files, both JS twins) carries a probe's expected FOL clause, or a quoted string holding all of a probe's content words (for zh, the characters). It is a separate test; the `whole_algorithm_values` and `CODE_TASK_OUTPUT_SURFACES` lists are unchanged. |
| R1186-10 | A probe set `data/benchmarks/formalization/{en,ru,hi,zh}.lino`, ten or more prompts each, with expected quantifier, predicates and FOL, covering universal, existential, negation and two-place relations. | Implemented: `data/benchmarks/formalization/{en,ru,hi,zh}.lino`, eleven probes each (universal, existential, negation and two-place relation), each with `expected_quantifier`, `expected_predicates` and `expected_fol`. `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_probe_set.rs` checks the coverage, the exact FOL of every probe and the round trip of every target; `rust/tests/web/issue-1186-formalization-probe-set.test.mjs` runs the same set against the browser worker. Hindi object-verb order needed a seeded `verb_final` grammar flag, pinned by `hindi_object_verb_order_reads_as_a_two_place_relation`. Listed in `docs/benchmarks.md`. |
